title: Arxo Findings Register
description: Verified discrepancies in legal texts, standards, official publications and implementations, with evidence and correction histories.

counts.rule: Counts are of findings. One finding is one independently checkable statement about one discrepancy at one place; classes and questions are counted separately and are not added together.

en.title: P.L. 119-21 §70204(a)(2)(A) quotes words that are not in 26 U.S.C. §529A(b)(2)(B)
en.summary: The amending instruction inserts new words after “except as provided in the case of contributions under subsection (c)(1)(C)”. Section 529A(b)(2)(B) reads “except in the case of contributions under subsection (c)(1)(C)”: the quoted words do not occur, as written in 2014 and kept in later amendments. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel executed the insertion after the existing words to reflect the probable intent of Congress.
en.impact: No consequence is claimed: the consolidated Code already reads as intended. The instruction itself cannot be executed as written.
en.correction: In §70204(a)(2)(A), strike “except as provided in the case of” and insert “except in the case of”.

quotes.source: Public Law 119-21, 139 Stat. 72 (govinfo USLM)
quotes.text: Section 529A(b)(2)(B) is amended by inserting “ or received in a qualified ABLE rollover contribution described in section 530A(d)(4)(B) ” after “ except as provided in the case of contributions under subsection (c)(1)(C) ”.

findings.location: Instructions for Form 6251 (2025), page 1, “Enhanced deduction for seniors”

en.title: Instructions for Form 6251 (2025) cite 26 U.S.C. §56(b)(5)(D), which does not exist
en.summary: The 2025 Instructions for Form 6251 say the enhanced deduction for seniors is treated as a personal exemption and added back to alternative minimum taxable income “as an adjustment under section 56(b)(5)(D)”. Section 56(b) has no paragraph (5); the disallowance of personal exemptions is in section 56(b)(1)(D).
en.impact: Citation only: the amount added back on the form is not affected.
en.correction: Cite section 56(b)(1)(D), subject to the publisher's confirmation.

en.title: 26 U.S.C. §42(e)(3)(B) refers to “subsection (b)(2)(B)(ii)”, which no longer exists
en.summary: Section 42(e)(3)(B) sets the credit for certain rehabilitation expenditures “using the percentage applicable under subsection (b)(2)(B)(ii)”. Subsection (b)(2)(B) has had no clauses since P.L. 110-289 §3002(a) restructured subsection (b); the 30 percent rule is now in subsection (b)(1)(B)(ii). The reference was not conformed when subsection (b) was rewritten.
en.correction: Refer to subsection (b)(1)(B)(ii).

findings.act: Grading instructions for farm animals, Order of the Minister of Agriculture of Kazakhstan No. 3-3/517 of 10 October 2014

en.title: Beef cattle grading, paragraph 28: class I is written as “81-70 points”, so totals of 61–70 fall into no class
en.summary: Paragraph 28 of the grading instructions for beef cattle sets “elite – 71-80 points”, “class I – 81-70 points” and “class II – 51-60 points”. A total of 61 to 70 points matches no row: a cow scoring 65 receives no class for the complex of traits. The Russian and Kazakh texts read the same way.
en.impact: An animal with a total of 61–70 points cannot be assigned a class for the complex of traits.
en.correction: “Class I – 61-70 points” (Kazakh text: “I сынып – 61-70 балл”).

quote_translations.ru: elite-record – 81 points and more; elite – 71-80 points; class I – 81-70 points; class II – 51-60 points
quote_translations.kk: elite – 71-80 points; class I – 81-70 points; class II – 51-60 points

ru.title: Мясной КРС, п. 28: границы I класса записаны как «81-70 баллов» — сумма 61–70 не попадает ни в один класс
ru.summary: В п. 28 Инструкции по бонитировке крупного рогатого скота мясного направления границы I класса записаны как «81-70 баллов». Соседние строки — «элита – 71-80 баллов» и «II класс – 51-60 баллов». Сумма от 61 до 70 баллов не попадает ни в одну строку: например, корова с суммой 65 баллов класса по комплексу признаков не получает. Так в русском и казахском текстах.

en.title: Maral and sika deer grading, paragraph 20: the weight threshold for class III hinds is “(ISO-IBS kg)” instead of a number
en.summary: Paragraph 20 of the grading instructions for marals and sika deer assigns to class III the hinds “with a very low live weight (ISO-IBS kg)”: a placeholder stands where the weight should be. Class II is 170–184 kg, so a hind below 170 kg cannot be classed by weight. The Russian and Kazakh texts read the same way.
en.impact: A hind weighing less than 170 kg falls into no weight class.
en.correction: For the issuing ministry to restore the value from the approved text of the order.

Второй класс — 170–184 кг, поэтому для матки с живой массой ниже 170 кг класс по массе не определяется. Так в русском и казахском текстах.

en.title: eCFR shows $84,852 in 11 CFR 111.24(a)(2)(ii); the January 2025 rule replaced it with $87,056
en.summary: The Federal Election Commission's 2025 inflation adjustment (90 FR 210, FR Doc. 2024-31368) amends section 111.24 by replacing the amount in paragraph (a)(2)(ii) with $87,056. The eCFR still shows the earlier $84,852 in its versions as of 31 December 2025 and 20 October 2026: the amendment to this paragraph was not incorporated.
en.impact: Anyone reading the eCFR sees a maximum penalty for a knowing and willful violation under paragraph (a)(2)(ii) that is $2,204 lower than the rule sets. No penalty actually assessed on the eCFR figure is claimed.
en.correction: $87,056, as set by the rule.

en.title: LFSS 2026 art. 18, II: the 2026 Finance Act cited under the number and date of the social security financing act itself (corrected on 23 May 2026)

en.title: CGI art. 199 sexdecies: the 2026 Finance Act replaces words that occur twice without saying which occurrence
en.summary: We applied article 29, 2°, of Law No. 2026-103 (2026 Finance Act) to the prior consolidated text of article 199 sexdecies of the General Tax Code. Point a) inserts a second occurrence of the words « de l'article D. 7231-1 du même code »; point b) then replaces those words with « du même II » without saying which occurrence, and the sentence in force refers to services « mentionnés au 16° du II du même II ». The discrepancy is in the adopted text itself: the final text adopted by the National Assembly (T.A. No. 227) and the authenticated Official Journal No. 0043 carry the same wording.
en.impact: No effect on the amount of the tax credit was identified; the intended reference (16° of II of article D. 7231-1 of the Labour Code) remains recognisable.
en.correction: A legislative coordination provision: in the second sentence of the second paragraph of 2 of article 199 sexdecies, replace « du II du même II » with « du même II ». A rectificatif cannot change wording that is in the adopted text.

quote_translations.instr-b: b) The words « of article D. 7231-1 of the same code » are replaced by the words « of the same II ».

fr.title: CGI, art. 199 sexdecies : la loi de finances pour 2026 remplace des mots qui figurent deux fois sans préciser l'occurrence
fr.summary: Nous avons appliqué l'article 29, 2°, de la loi n° 2026-103 de finances pour 2026 à la version consolidée antérieure de l'article 199 sexdecies du code général des impôts. Le a) insère une seconde occurrence des mots « de l'article D. 7231-1 du même code » ; le b) remplace ensuite ces mots par « du même II » sans préciser l'occurrence, et la phrase en vigueur vise les services « mentionnés au 16° du II du même II ». L'écart est dans le texte adopté : le texte définitif de l'Assemblée nationale (T.A. n° 227) et le JO authentique n° 0043 portent la même rédaction.
fr.impact: Aucun effet sur le montant du crédit d'impôt n'a été identifié ; la référence voulue (16° du II de l'article D. 7231-1 du code du travail) reste reconnaissable.
fr.correction: Une disposition législative de coordination : à la seconde phrase du deuxième alinéa du 2 de l'article 199 sexdecies, remplacer « du II du même II » par « du même II ». Un rectificatif ne peut pas modifier une rédaction qui figure dans le texte adopté.

en.title: LFSS 2026 art. 102, II, 3°: the title of Law No. 2025-199 misquoted as « de financement pour la sécurité sociale »
en.summary: Article 102, II, 3°, of Law No. 2025-1403 (2026 social security financing act) cites « la loi n° 2025-199 du 28 février 2025 de financement pour la sécurité sociale pour 2025 ». en.title: CSS art. L. 136-4, IV, on Légifrance: the word « aux » dropped and « définiaux » run together after the 2026 social security financing act
en.summary: We applied article 18, I, 2°, of Law No. 2025-1403 to the prior consolidated version of article L. 136-4, IV, of the Social Security Code and compared the result with the versions published on Légifrance (LEGIARTI000053282498 from 31 December 2025 and LEGIARTI000053284767 in force since 21 February 2026). The instruction replaces only « mêmes articles 64 bis et 76 », so the result reads « déterminés aux articles 50-0, 64 bis, 76 et 102 ter » and « du champ défini aux articles »; both versions read « déterminés articles » and « définiaux ». The discrepancy arose in the consolidation; the text published in the Official Journal is correct.
en.correction: In both versions, read « du champ défini aux articles » and « déterminés aux articles 50-0, 64 bis, 76 et 102 ter du même code ».

en.title: CGI art. 1600 on Légifrance, version for 2027: the 2026 Finance Act insertion on the Corsica chamber of commerce is missing
en.summary: Article 135, VI, A, of Law No. 2026-103 (2026 Finance Act) inserts « et l'établissement public du commerce et de l'industrie de Corse » after « région » in I of article 1600 of the General Tax Code, with no end date. en.title: CSS art. L. 162-23-8 on Légifrance, version from 1 September 2027: both changes made by the 2026 social security financing act are missing
en.summary: Article 72, I, 5°, of Law No. 2025-1403 deletes « part prévue au 2° du I de l'article L. 162-23, affectée à la » from the first paragraph of I of article L. 162-23-8 of the Social Security Code and inserts « exerçant les activités mentionnées au 4° du même article L. 162-22 ». The version in force until 1 September 2027 (LEGIARTI000053283299) contains both changes; the version from 1 September 2027 (LEGIARTI000048971734, which stems from Law No. 2023-29) contains none of them and restores the earlier wording. The discrepancy arose in the consolidation; the text published in the Official Journal is correct.
en.correction: Rebuild the version from 1 September 2027 with both changes of article 72, I, 5°, keeping the change made by Law No. 2023-29 in 1°.

en.title: 2026 energy taxation guide: the ED95 rate is 12.119 €/MWh on page 25 but 12.157 €/MWh on pages 33 and 37
en.summary: We compared the « Guide 2026 sur la fiscalité des énergies » published by the Ministry of Ecological Transition (editions of 30 May and 22 July 2026) with article L. 312-79 of the Code of taxes on goods and services (CIBS). Page 25 and article L. 312-79 give 12.119 €/MWh for ethanol-diesel ED95, while page 33 (annex 2) and page 37 (annex 3, 6.43 €/hL) give 12.157 €/MWh, although 6.43 × 3.6 / 1.91 = 12.119. The discrepancy is in the guide; the rate in the code is not affected.
en.correction: On pages 33 and 37, read 12.119 €/MWh.

findings.act: Grading instructions for farm animals, Order of the Minister of Agriculture of Kazakhstan No. 3-3/517 of 10 October 2014

en.title: Rabbit grading, paragraph 10: the Russian and Kazakh texts set opposite culling conditions
en.summary: The Russian text of paragraph 10 recommends culling does “that raised fewer than 5 kits in each of the first two kindlings” and those with “more than two consecutive misses”. The Kazakh text of the same paragraph names does that raised “at least 5 kits” and misses “twice in a row”. The condition on the number of kits is reversed between the language versions, and the number of misses differs.
en.impact: Read literally, the Kazakh text recommends culling the more productive does.
en.correction: Kazakh text: “5-тен кем көжек өсірген”; the number of misses to be aligned in both versions by the issuing ministry.

quote_translations.ru: does that raised fewer than 5 kits in each of the first two kindlings (except where caused by sterile bucks)
quote_translations.ru-2: more than two consecutive misses have been recorded
quote_translations.kk: a doe that raised at least 5 kits in each of its first two kindlings
quote_translations.kk-2: if she has not conceived twice in a row

ru.title: Кролики, п. 10: русский и казахский тексты дают противоположные условия выбраковки
ru.summary: Русский текст п. 10 рекомендует выбраковывать самок, «вырастивших менее 5 крольчат в каждом из двух первых окролов», и крольчих с «более двух последовательных пропустований». Казахский текст того же пункта говорит «кем дегенде 5 көжекті өсірген аналық» (вырастивших не менее 5 крольчат) и «қатарынан екі рет буаз болмаса» (два раза подряд). Условие по числу крольчат в языковых версиях противоположное, число пропустований различается.
ru.correction: Казахский текст: «5-тен кем көжек өсірген»; число пропустований согласовать в обеих версиях.

kk.title: Қояндар, 10-тармақ: орыс және қазақ мәтіндері жарамсызға шығарудың қарама-қарсы шарттарын береді
kk.summary: 10-тармақтың орыс мәтіні «алғашқы екі көжектеуінің әрқайсысында 5-тен кем көжек өсірген» аналықтарды және «қатарынан екіден артық» буаз болмаған аналықтарды жарамсызға шығаруды ұсынады. Сол тармақтың қазақ мәтінінде «кем дегенде 5 көжекті өсірген аналық» және «қатарынан екі рет буаз болмаса» деп жазылған. Көжек саны бойынша шарт тіл нұсқаларында қарама-қарсы, буаз болмау саны әртүрлі.
kk.correction: Қазақ мәтіні: «5-тен кем көжек өсірген»; буаз болмау санын екі нұсқада келісу.

en.title: Rev. Proc. 2025-32: the 2026 head-of-household standard deduction is published as $24,150; the statutory rounding rule gives $24,175
en.summary: Section 63(c)(7)(B)(ii) increases the $23,625 base by the cost-of-living adjustment and rounds the increase down to the next lowest multiple of $50. With the C-CPI-U values published on 11 September 2025 the increase is $559.56, rounded to $550, giving $24,175. Rev. Proc. 2025-32, section 4.14(1), publishes $24,150: its increase of $525 is not a multiple of $50 and matches rounding the whole amount instead of the increase.
en.impact: The 2026 standard deduction of a head-of-household filer is $25 lower than the amount the statute gives. This is a difference in the deduction, not in tax: the tax effect depends on the filer's bracket.

en.title: Rev. Proc. 2025-32: the 2026 section 6334(d)(4)(B) amount is published as $5,300; the statutory rounding rule gives $5,250
en.summary: Section 6334(d)(4)(C) increases the $4,150 amount by the cost-of-living adjustment (base year 2017) and rounds the increase down to a multiple of $100. For 2026 the increase is $1,167.12, rounded to $1,100, giving $5,250. Rev. Proc. 2025-32 publishes $5,300 in section 4.50 (wages exempt from levy) and section 4.35 (qualified disability trust deduction, which uses the same adjustment); the published increase, $1,150, is not a multiple of $100 and matches rounding the full amount, $5,317.12, down. Rev. Proc. 2024-40 shows the same pattern for 2025 in sections 2.35 and 2.51: $5,100 published, $5,150 under the statute.
en.impact: The per-dependent amount used to compute wages exempt from levy is $50 higher than the statute gives for 2026 and was $50 lower for 2025; holding the standard deduction constant, that is about $0.96 per dependent per week. The qualified disability trust deduction differs by the same $50.
en.correction: $5,250 for 2026, or a published statement of the authority for rounding the whole amount.

en.title: FEES Schedule 1, 1.1-1: the exception for Operating a Digital Asset Trading Facility is printed but was never enacted
en.summary: Amendments No. 14.1 (9 December 2023) inserted 1.1-1 (additional application fee for Digital Assets activities) without an exception; the same instrument put an exception for Operating a Digital Asset Trading Facility only into 6.1-1. Consolidated versions V15 to V18 print the exception in 1.1-1 as well, and we could not find it in any of the published amending instruments Nos. 12 to 17. The draft in Consultation Paper AFSA-PSRD-CSP-2026-0004 amends 1.1-1 again (the fixed amount is replaced by a table) and prints the words "except for the Regulated Activity of Operating a Digital Asset Trading Facility" as existing text, not as an insertion.
en.correction: Since the draft amends 1.1-1 in any case, please either enact the exception expressly in the amending instrument, as new text, or remove it, and identify the instrument that supports it for the period since V15.

en.title: PRU (Investment Firms) Table 3.3: a manager of a Single Family Office Fund without a custodian falls in two rows (USD 50,000 and USD 500,000)
en.summary: Amendments No. 4 (in force 1 July 2024) added "or (b) because the Fund is a Single Family Office Fund" to the USD 50,000 row of Table 3.3. The USD 500,000 row for a Collective Investment Scheme "which does not have an appointed Eligible Custodian" was not changed; its only exception is the nature of the Fund and its assets. A manager of a Single Family Office Fund without an Eligible Custodian therefore meets both rows, and the text does not say which applies. Reading both rows cumulatively gives USD 500,000 and leaves the limb added by Amendments No. 4 without effect.
en.correction: Please clarify which row applies to a Single Family Office Fund without an Eligible Custodian and, if USD 50,000 is intended, exclude that case expressly from the USD 500,000 row.

en.title: PRU (Investment Firms) 1.3(10) and 6.1(2): which Chapter 6 rules apply to Externally Regulated firms
en.summary: Rule 1.3(10) says that "in Chapter 6, only Rule 6.6 applies" to Externally Regulated PRU Investment Firms. Rule 6.1(2) says "Other than Rules 6.5 and 6.6, this Chapter does not apply" to them, and Rule 6.5(2) contains a limitation written for them. en.correction: Please align PRU INV 1.3(10) with 6.1(2) and 6.5(2) by addressing both Rules 6.5 and 6.6 expressly.

en.title: The Structure of the Bodies of the AIFC, §9(14): the Governor recommends judges "to the Council"
en.summary: Under Article 13(3-1) of the Constitutional Statute the Chairman and judges of the AIFC Court are appointed by the President on the Governor's recommendation; the AIFC Court Regulations say the same. §9(14) of the Structure of the Bodies (as of 1 July 2021) says that the Governor recommends to the Council the persons to be appointed as judges, wording that predates the 2017 amendment of the Statute.
en.correction: Please clarify the role of the Council in §9(14), consistently with appointment by the President on the Governor's recommendation.

en.title: AFSA online COB does not include the Amendments No. 14 changes in force since 13 January 2026
en.summary: Amendments No. 14 to COB commence on 13 January 2026, except the changes to COB 1.2.2, which commenced on 13 October 2025. The consolidated version V17 on aifc.kz contains them: COB 8.1.2 and 8.1.4 now cover firms that Provide Money Services, the Guidance under COB 8.2.5 refers to PMS 9, COB 15.1 has two new paragraphs, and the new COB 15.5 sets a deadline of 15 business days for Money Service complaints. The aifc.kz page for COB says that the current version can be found on the regulator's website. The AFSA online COB (checked on 23 October 2026) shows none of these changes: COB 8.1.2(a) still refers only to Investment Business, COB 15.1 has one paragraph, and there is no COB 15.5. The page shows no deleted (struck-through) text at these places.
en.correction: Please update the online COB to include the amendments in force since 13 January 2026, including COB 8.1.2, 8.1.4, 15.1 and 15.5.

en.summary: COB 1.2.4 disapplies COB to Trust Service Providers except, among others, "COB 15 (Record Keeping)". Chapter 15 is "Complaints Handling and Dispute Resolution"; Chapter 16 is "Record Keeping and Internal Audit"; and section 15.4 inside Chapter 15 is "Record keeping" for complaints. The number and the label point to different provisions. The mismatch exists from the first version of COB (2017) and was kept through every later change to 1.2.4. Other exclusion rules name the chapters correctly, for example 1.2.2(g): "COB 15 (Complaints Handling and Dispute Resolution), COB 16 (Record Keeping and Internal Audit)".
en.correction: Please state which rules apply to Trust Service Providers: (1) COB 15 (Complaints Handling and Dispute Resolution); (2) COB 16 (Record Keeping and Internal Audit); (3) both; or (4) COB 15.4 (Record keeping), the complaint-records section of COB 15.

en.title: MAR 1.1.2(1)(b): is an offer that meets both (2)(c) and (2)(d) meant to lose the placement exemption?
en.summary: MAR 1.1.2(1)(b) exempts an offer by way of placement only if it satisfies "one and one only" of the conditions in (2); (1)(c) allows combinations only where one of them is (a), (b) or (m). An offer of Securities denominated in units of at least USD 100,000 (condition (d)) and issued at or above that amount also meets condition (c), because every investor pays at least USD 100,000. Read literally, such an offer is not exempt unless it also meets (a), (b) or (m), while the same offer issued below USD 100,000 per unit would be. For Exempt Securities, MAR 1.2.2(1) uses "one or more of the conditions". The words "one and one only" may be meant to stop the stacking of exemptions, but the text does not say which combinations are excluded.
en.correction: Please confirm whether an offer that meets both conditions 1.1.2(2)(c) and (d) is meant to lose the exemption unless 1.1.2(1)(c) applies. If not, please consider "one or more of the conditions", or name the conditions that may not be combined.

en.title: MAR 2.4.5(b) refers to "a Takeover Offer under the Takeover Rules": which Takeover Rules apply?
en.summary: MAR 2.4.5(b) lifts the closed-period dealing ban for "undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a Takeover Offer under the Takeover Rules". The Glossary defines "Takeover Rules" as Rules prescribed by the AFSA under section 88(1)(a) of the Framework Regulations, which says that the AFSA "may prescribe" such Rules. We did not find any Takeover Rules among the acts published on aifc.kz or in the AFSA online rulebook. Chapter 11 of Part 7 of the AIFC Companies Regulations ("Protection of Minorities in Takeovers") is part of the Regulations, not Rules made by the AFSA under section 88(1)(a). If no Takeover Rules have been made, exemption (b) has nothing to apply to, and a Restricted Person would need clearance under MAR 2.4.4.
en.correction: Please identify the Takeover Rules that apply for MAR 2.4.5(b), or confirm that this exemption currently has no application. If it is meant to apply now, please consider referring simply to "a Takeover Offer", which the Glossary defines.

en.title: REC 1.1.4(a): should the comparison also cover Chapter 2 of Part 3 of the Framework Regulations?
en.summary: REC 1.1.4 is made for section 89(3)(a) of the Framework Regulations, which asks whether investors get protection equivalent to the requirements for licensing an Authorised Market Institution "in Chapter 2 of Part 3". REC 1.1.4(a) asks the applicant to compare its home rules "with Part 4 of the Framework Regulations and Chapters 2 and 3 or 4 (as appropriate) of the AMI Rules". Part 4 is "Controlled and Designated Functions". The AMI chapters cover much of what section 89(3)(a) protects, and controlled functions are also relevant, but Chapter 2 of Part 3 is not named.
en.correction: Please clarify whether REC 1.1.4(a) should also refer to, or refer instead to, Chapter 2 of Part 3 of the Framework Regulations.

en.title: AFSA online Market Rules do not contain MAR 1.9.3 and 1.9.4 (Amendments No. 7, 29 June 2022)
en.summary: The AFSA online Market Rules do not contain MAR 1.9.3 (Expert’s responsibility) and 1.9.4 (Exceptions from liability), which Amendments No. 7 inserted with effect from 29 June 2022. In the online text, 1.9.2 (Limitations on the application of MAR 1.9.1) is followed directly by 1.10 (AIFC ESG Debentures). The consolidated versions V8 to V13 on aifc.kz contain both rules. The online text applied another change made by the same instrument (MAR 2.1(2), which excludes Listed Funds and Exempt Offerors from MAR 2), but not its change to MAR 3.1-1(1), which in the act also excludes an Exempt Offeror from MAR 3. The online Schedule 4, paragraph 1(a)(ii) still refers to "consent under MAR 1.9.3", and the Glossary defines "Expert" by MAR 1.9.3; a reader of the online rulebook cannot find that rule. Our earlier observation on the Glossary entry "Expert" (AIFC-GLO-06) relied on the online text and is withdrawn: the definition resolves in the act. MAR 1.9.4(4)(a) has a separate wrong reference (see AIFC2-MKT-05).
en.correction: Please insert MAR 1.9.3 and 1.9.4 in the online Market Rules and apply the change to MAR 3.1-1(1) made by Amendments No. 7.

en.title: COB 1.2.2(c) applies COB 8 (Client Assets) to Authorised Crowdfunding Platforms, but the reading rule does not reach the scope of COB 8, which is defined by Investment Business
en.summary: COB 1.2.2(c) disapplies COB for an Authorised Crowdfunding Platform except COB 3, COB 4, COB 7, "COB 8 (Client Assets)" and COB Schedule 2, and the reading rule that follows provides that in these chapters "Regulated Activities" shall be read as "Market Activities". COB 8 does not use that term to set its scope: it applies to a firm that holds Money for a Client "in the course of, or in connection with, the carrying on of Investment Business or Provides Money Services" (COB 8.1.2(a), 8.1.4), and COB 8.2.1 defines Client Money by Investment Business. Operating a Loan or Investment Crowdfunding Platform is a Market Activity and is not in the Glossary definition of Investment Business. Read literally, the Client Money Rules do not attach to money a platform holds for lenders or investors, for example before the target funding amount is reached (AMI 7.3.22) or when it collects repayments for lenders (AMI 7.4.2), unless the platform also holds a licence for Investment Business or Money Services (AMI 7.2.1). AMI 2.9.1 requires satisfactory arrangements for safeguarding users' assets, and AMI 7.3.4(1)(n) requires disclosure of the "arrangements and safeguards for Client Assets held or controlled by an Authorised Crowdfunding Platform", but these rules do not set out the client money rules or the distribution rules in COB 8.2.16. Example: lenders transfer 900,000 USD to a platform for a loan with a target of 1,000,000 USD; the platform fails before the target is reached; whether the 900,000 USD is Client Money protected by COB 8.2.16 depends on whether COB 8 is read as reaching Market Activities.
en.correction: Please add to the reading rules for COB 1.2.2(c) that references in COB 8 to "Investment Business" are read as references to the Market Activities of an Authorised Crowdfunding Platform, or otherwise state how COB 8 applies to money held by such platforms.

en.title: Disclosure item for a Fund Manager acting itself as custodian of Real Property points to CIS 7.3(e), which the same amending instrument deleted
en.summary: CIS 5.3(l)(viii) requires three disclosures "If the Fund Manager itself acts as the custodian of Real Property, in accordance with CIS 7.3.(e)". CIS 7.3(e) reads "[intentionally omitted]": Amendments No. 3 (in force 1 June 2023) inserted 5.3(l)(viii) with this reference and, on the same page, deleted the whole of 7.3(e), which was the custody exemption for a Self-managed Fund. The reference therefore has no target. A Fund may still have no Eligible Custodian under 8.2(b), or under a waiver (8.2(e) or 1.3), but CIS does not describe any of these cases as the Fund Manager itself acting as custodian, so it is unclear when the disclosure applies. The draft in Consultation Paper AFSA-PSRD-CSP-2026-0001 deletes the words "Subject to Rule (e), and" in 7.3(d) but moves the disclosure item, with the same reference to 7.3(e), into the new CIS 5.6.2(h).
en.correction: Please state which case the item (5.3(l)(viii), in the draft 5.6.2(h)) is meant to cover and correct the reference: (a) to CIS 8.2(b) or 8.2(e), if those cases are meant; or (b) to a new rule that allows a Fund Manager to act as custodian of Real Property, with conditions. If no such case is intended, the item can be removed.

en.title: CIS 5.1 disapplies 5.3(b)(i) (investment objective, strategy, leverage) for Non-Exempt Funds; in the draft, 5.1 refers to the deleted rule 5.3
en.summary: CIS 5.1(a) applies 5.3 to all Funds "excluding 5.3(b)(i) and (j)", and 5.1(b) applies "5.3(b)(i) and (j)" to Exempt Funds only. 5.3(b)(i) is the core disclosure of the investment objective, policy and strategy, asset types, risks and leverage, including the maximum level of leverage. The items that are Exempt-only by nature are 5.3(i) (the Exempt Fund legend) and 5.3(j) (the legend for an Exempt Fund of a Foreign Fund Manager). Read literally, a Non-Exempt (retail) Fund is relieved of 5.3(b)(i) while Exempt Funds must give it. The opening words of 5.3(b) and Schedule 1(j) still bind every Fund, so what is literally lost is the specific list, including the maximum level of leverage. The draft in Consultation Paper AFSA-PSRD-CSP-2026-0001 deletes rule 5.3 and moves its content to the new 5.4, 5.5 and Schedule 1-1, while 5.1(a) and (b) still refer to "5.3 (excluding 5.3(b)(i) and (j))" and "5.3(b)(i) and (j)". If the draft is adopted as published, both references will point to a deleted rule.
en.correction: Please confirm whether 5.1(a) and (b) should refer to the Exempt Fund legends (5.3(i) and (j)) rather than to 5.3(b)(i). When finalising the draft, please redirect 5.1(a) and (b) to the new content rules (5.4 and 5.5) and name the items that apply to Exempt Funds only.

en.title: Custody for domestic Exempt Funds: CIS 7.3(d) requires an Eligible Custodian "in accordance with Rule 8.2", but chapter 8 applies only to other Funds; do its exceptions apply?
en.summary: CIS chapter 7 applies to Domestic Fund Managers "in respect of all Funds" (7.1), so 7.3(d) — delegate custody to an Eligible Custodian "in accordance with Rule 8.2" — reaches domestic Exempt Funds. Chapter 8, including the exceptions in 8.2(b) and (e), applies only to Non-Exempt Funds and REITs of Domestic Fund Managers and to Exempt Funds of Foreign Fund Managers (8.1). The words "in accordance with Rule 8.2" can be read to bring the exceptions in 8.2(b) and (e) with them, and the general waiver in CIS 1.3 is also available, but the text does not say so. Separately, PRU(INV) Table 3.3 assumes that a Single Family Office Fund does not need an Eligible Custodian; CIS has no such rule. This overlaps with our earlier item on PRU(INV) Table 3.3 (AIFC-PRU-01).
en.correction: Please state whether 8.2(b) and (e) apply to Exempt Funds of Domestic Fund Managers and, if a Single Family Office Fund may operate without an Eligible Custodian, set that out in CIS.

en.title: Reports on Single Family Office and Corporate Treasury Centre Funds: the draft extends CIS 10.4 and 10.5 to every Domestic Fund, but 10.5(b) and the Guidance to 2.4.17 do not match
en.summary: Under the current CIS, reports on Single Family Office and Corporate Treasury Centre Funds (10.5-1(j), 10.5-1.1) have no deadline, frequency or recipient: both Funds must be Exempt Funds, and 10.5, which sets the timing and recipients of Fund reports, applies to Non-Exempt Funds only (10.1(ii)). CIS also does not require these Funds to be audited (10.4 and 10.1(i)). The draft in Consultation Paper AFSA-PSRD-CSP-2026-0001 extends the audit rule in 10.4 and the periodic reports in 10.5(a) to each Domestic Fund, which answers most of this point. Two questions remain on the draft. First, 10.5(b) still sets the four-month deadline for the annual report "for the Non-Exempt Fund", while 10.5(c) no longer says "Non-Exempt", so the deadline for the annual report of other Domestic Funds is unclear. Second, the Guidance to the new 2.4.17 says that for a Corporate Treasury Centre Fund "the standard Fund Manager reporting requirements under CIS 10.5 also do not apply", while the draft 10.5(a) covers each Domestic Fund and states no exception.
en.correction: When finalising the draft, please make 10.5(b) cover every Fund to which 10.5(a) applies (for example "for the Fund", as in 10.5(c)), and either state in the rules that 10.5 does not apply to Corporate Treasury Centre Funds, with the reporting that replaces it, or align the Guidance to 2.4.17 with 10.5(a).

en.title: IFR 7.5(3) and the draft Shari'ah Governance Rules: does a Fund that relies on Shari'ah screening keep its relief from appointing an SSB?
en.summary: Under the current IFR, 7.5(3) releases the Fund Manager of a Non-Exempt Fund from appointing an SSB where it relies on a widely accepted Shari'ah screening process, while 7.3(1), 7.6(2) and 7.7(1) refer to "the Fund's SSB" without an exception. The draft in Consultation Paper AFSA-PSRD-CSP-2026-0003 deletes IFR 7.5 to 7.7 and places Shari'ah governance in new Shari'ah Governance Rules, which apply to "a Fund Manager of a Domestic Fund which is operated or held out as being operated as an Islamic Fund" (rule 1(1)(b)). After adoption the conflict inside IFR falls away with 7.5 to 7.7. Two questions remain: the new Rules contain no counterpart of the screening relief in 7.5(3), so it is unclear whether such Funds must now appoint an SSB; and IFR 7.3(1), which the draft does not amend, still requires approval by "the Fund's SSB".
en.correction: When finalising the draft, please state whether a Fund that relies on a widely accepted Shari'ah screening process keeps its relief from appointing an SSB under the new Shari'ah Governance Rules, and align IFR 7.3(1) with the answer (for example "where an SSB is appointed to the Fund").

en.title: IFR 7.3 requires SSB approval of a Fund's "Prospectus", a Glossary term for securities prospectuses; Funds issue "Offering Materials"

In the Glossary, "Prospectus" is the document referred to in MAR 1.3, which an unlisted Fund does not issue; such a Fund gives investors "Offering Materials" (CIS 5.3), and IFR itself uses that term in 7.8. CIS has moved to the same term for Funds: Amendments No. 7 to CIS (in force 1 January 2025) replaced "Prospectus" with "Offering Materials" in the Feeder Fund rules. IFR 7.3 was not aligned.
en.correction: Please use "Offering Materials" in IFR 7.3(1), 7.3(2) and the Guidance under 7.2, or state that "Prospectus" there includes a Fund’s Offering Materials.

en.title: Non-significant investments: holdings below 10% of CET1 are deducted in full, holdings at or above 10% only above the threshold
en.summary: BBR 4.29(4) applies when, after other regulatory adjustments, the total of the deductions under that rule is less than 10% of the Bank's CET1 capital; the Bank must then deduct the investments in full (4.29(4)(b)-(c)). BBR 4.29(5) applies when the total is 10% or more and deducts only the amount by which it exceeds 10% (the excess). With CET1 of 100, holdings of 9.9 are deducted in full (9.9), holdings of 10 lead to no deduction and holdings of 11 to a deduction of 1. A bank can therefore keep more CET1 by holding more. IBB 4.43 and 4.44 have the same structure. Carried through to the capital ratios: for a bank with CET1 of USD 50 million, other credit risk-weighted assets of USD 450 million, a market risk requirement of USD 4 million and an operational risk requirement of USD 7.5 million, holdings of USD 4.9 million are deducted in full and the bank falls below its capital requirement under 4.9 and the 8% Total Capital ratio (USD 45.1 million against 47.5 million); holdings of USD 5.0 million are not deducted and the bank meets them (USD 50 million against 48.7 million). Line 37 of Form 30 in the Manual for Preparation of Returns deducts only the amount above the 10% threshold.
en.correction: Please clarify how much is deducted below and at or above the 10% threshold, so that the deduction does not fall when holdings rise. For example: (a) deduct only the amount above 10% of CET1 and risk-weight the holdings below it, or (b) keep full deduction and apply it at every level.

en.title: Basic indicator approach: GI is defined as an average, and the formula divides it by n again
en.summary: BBR 7.6(2) sets the operational risk capital requirement as GI x alpha / n. GI is defined as "the Bank's average annual gross income" for the years (out of the previous 3) in which it is positive, and n is the number of those years. The average is therefore divided by n a second time, and the result falls as the number of positive years grows: with gross income of USD 50 million in each of three years the requirement is 50 x 15% / 3 = USD 2.5 million; with USD 50 million in one year and losses in the other two it is USD 7.5 million. Sub-rule (3) speaks of excluding loss years "from both the numerator and denominator when calculating the average". The difference concerns the operational risk component, which enters risk-weighted assets at 12.5 times the requirement (BBR 4.7(2)(b)), not the whole capital requirement. IBB 9.10(2) has the same formula and definition. Carried through to the capital ratios: for a bank with gross income of USD 50 million in each of three years, other credit risk-weighted assets of USD 450 million, a market risk requirement of USD 4 million and Total Capital of USD 45 million, the requirement under 4.9 is USD 42.5 million as printed and USD 47.5 million if gross income is averaged once, so the bank meets or breaches the 8% Total Capital ratio depending on the reading (8.47% against 7.58%). The AFSA return (Annex 1.13 of the Manual for Preparation of Returns) computes a single "Average GI" over the positive years and does not divide it by n again.
en.correction: Please confirm that the requirement is meant to equal alpha times the average of the positive annual gross income figures. If so, please define GI in BBR 7.6(2) and IBB 9.10(2) as the sum of those figures, or delete the division by n.

en.title: Securitisation exposures: Table 5C row 10 or Table 5H? No rule says which applies to an originator's or sponsor's retained positions
en.summary: BBR has two risk-weight tables for securitisation exposures. Table 5B item 9 sends "claims on securitisation exposures" to Table 5C row 10 (50% to 250%; unrated 150%). Rule 5.21(16) applies Table 5H (20% to 350%; B+ and below or unrated 1,250% or deduction) to on-balance-sheet retained securitisation exposures, which 5.21(12)-(13) link to a Bank that is an originator or sponsor, including its investments in the securitisation. Read as a specific rule, 5.21(16) governs those positions and Table 5C row 10 the positions of other investors. But no rule says so, and 5.21(7) speaks of applying Table 5H to "a securitisation exposure" in general. The weights differ widely, for example 50% against 20% for AAA and 150% against 1,250% for an unrated exposure.
en.correction: Please confirm which table applies to which securitisation positions: Table 5H only to retained exposures of an originator or sponsor (5.21(16)), or to all securitisation exposures where the due-diligence conditions of 5.21(7) are met; and state this in Table 5B item 9 or in 5.21.

en.title: Allocation of the 10% excess across tiers uses the bank's OWN capital as numerator and holdings as denominator; shares do not sum to 1
en.summary: BBR 4.29(5)(c) allocates the excess over 10% to each tier of capital by the formula Excess x A/B, where A is "the amount of CET 1 capital, additional tier 1 capital or tier 2 capital of the Bank" and B is "the total capital holdings of the Bank". Read literally, A is the bank's own capital in a tier, while B is its holdings in other entities, so the three shares do not add up to 1. For example, with own CET1, AT1 and T2 of 100, 10 and 20, holdings of 12 (CET1) and 3 (T2) and an excess of 5, the literal formula deducts 43.3 in total instead of 5. Under 4.29(1)(b) deductions are made from the tier for which the held capital would qualify, which points to A being the bank's holdings in that tier. "Capital holdings" is not defined. IBB 4.44(3) has the same wording. With holdings of USD 15 million, all in CET1 instruments, and own CET1 of USD 100 million, the literal formula deducts USD 33.3 million instead of 5 million; with holdings of USD 150 million it deducts USD 93.3 million instead of 140 million. For a bank with other credit risk-weighted assets of USD 900 million, a market risk requirement of USD 10 million and an operational risk requirement of USD 15 million (capital requirement USD 99.4 million), Total Capital after the allocation is USD 86.7 million under the literal formula and USD 125 million if A is the holdings of each tier.
en.correction: Please define A as the Bank's holdings of CET1, AT1 or T2 instruments of the entities concerned (as the case may be) and B as the total of those holdings, in BBR 4.29(5)(c) and IBB 4.44(3).

en.title: Threshold deduction: 10% per item 'or' 15% aggregate; (4) deducts the excess over '(3)(a) or (b)' - outcome indeterminate
en.summary: 4.30(3) grants full recognition (300%/400% risk weight, no deduction) 'provided that (a) each item is no more than 10% ...; or (b) in total, the 3 items are no more than 15%'. With 'or', a bank whose items are each under 10% but total over 15% satisfies (a) and needs no deduction, while 4.30(4) requires deduction of 'any amount in excess of the threshold in (3)(a) or (b)', which can be read as the excess over 15%. The same 'or' is in IBB 4.46(3). (Also '(net of all regulatory adjustments except those under this Subdivision)': there are no Subdivisions in BBR.) With three items of USD 9 million each and CET1 of USD 100 million, the text yields a deduction of 0 (sub-rule (3)(a)) and of USD 12 million (sub-rule (4) by reference to (3)(b)). A bank with other credit risk-weighted assets of USD 800 million and a market risk requirement of USD 10 million then both meets and breaches its capital requirement under 4.9 (USD 100 million against 97.64 million; USD 88 million against 93.8 million). Lines 38-40 and 44 of Form 30 in the Manual for Preparation of Returns apply the 10% and 15% limits together.
en.correction: Please make the two caps work together: either (a) replace "or" in 4.30(3) with "and" and deduct the amount above each 10% cap and then the amount above the 15% aggregate cap, or (b) keep alternative caps and state in 4.30(4) which excess is deducted. IBB 4.46(3) needs the same change.

en.title: Table 4A capital conservation ratios: rows share boundary values ('to' / '≥') and 7.0% sits between '≥6.375% to 7.0%' and '>7%'
en.summary: BBR Table 4A uses the bands "4.5% to 5.125%", "≥5.125% to 5.75%", "≥5.75% to 6.375%", "≥6.375% to 7.0%" and ">7%". IBB Table 5.1 uses "X% or more but less than Y%" and "≥7%".
en.correction: Please write the bands as "X% or more but less than Y%" and the last row as "≥7%" (as in IBB Table 5.1), and align BPG paragraph 11.

en.title: BPG not updated: it says Credit Providers are not Banking Business firms and excludes them from the leverage ratio, which BBR 4.36 has applied to Providing Credit since December 2022
en.summary: BPG paragraph 6 says: "Credit Providers as defined in BBR 1.7 are not included in Banking Business firms according to BBR 1.4." BBR 1.4(3) has said since 2018 that a Banking Business firm may be a Credit Provider, and BPG paragraphs 2, 4 and 5 themselves include Credit Providers. The BPG tables also exclude Credit Providers from Section 4F (Rules 4.36-4.37, leverage ratio). That matched BBR 4.36 until the version with amendments as of 9 December 2022, which applies Section 4F to firms licensed for "Accepting Deposits" or "Providing Credit". The BPG (28 January 2019) has not been updated. The BBR prevail, so the problem is misleading guidance.
en.correction: Please delete BPG paragraph 6 and remove the Credit Provider exclusion from Section 4F (Rules 4.36-4.37) in the BPG tables.

en.title: Relief from the asset risk charge for assets excluded from Eligible Capital "in accordance with the table B1": the phrase can be read two ways (PINS and TRR)
en.summary: PINS Schedule 5, paragraph 4.4: an insurer "need not include an amount in the asset risk charge for any asset excluded from Eligible Capital in accordance with the table B1 in paragraph 4.1". Table B1 sets charges and excludes nothing from Eligible Capital; the exclusions are in Schedule 3, paragraph 5. If the words "in accordance with the table B1" go with "the asset risk charge", the relief covers assets excluded under Schedule 3, which is the evident purpose. If they go with "excluded", the relief covers no asset. TRR Schedule 5, paragraph 4.4 is the same.
en.correction: Please make the reference clear, for example "... for any asset excluded from Eligible Capital under paragraph 5 of Schedule 3", in both rulebooks.

en.title: General insurers must seek MER advice from "its Approved Actuary"; it is unclear whether insurers not otherwise required to have one must appoint one (PINS and TRR)
en.summary: PINS Schedule 5, paragraph 10 applies to General Insurance Business. Paragraph 10.2(2) requires an insurer to "seek advice from its Approved Actuary" about its maximum event retention if it issues policies without a maximum amount insured, insures risks in multiple lines of business or has a complex portfolio. Under PINS 2.2.2(2) an Approved Actuary is mandatory for a general insurer only in certain cases, and PINS 9.2 deals with insurers "not required to have an Approved Actuary". The text does not say whether paragraph 10.2(2) itself requires such an insurer to appoint one, or whether it may use the independent actuary described in PINS 9.2.3. TRR Schedule 5, paragraph 10.2(2) is the same.
en.correction: Please clarify whether an insurer subject to Schedule 5 paragraph 10.2(2), but outside rule 2.2.2(2), must appoint an Approved Actuary or may use the actuary described in rule 9.2.3 (and the same for TRR).

en.title: TRR: Takaful Fund ring-fence exceptions refer to a non-existent "Rule 2.1.2 (1)", 2.2.3 to "rule 2.1.1", and 1.1.3(2) to 1.1.6(1) for the definition of Takaful Business

TRR 2.1 ("Overall Governance") has no numbered sub-rules. Separately, 1.1.3(2) refers to Takaful Business "as defined in Rules 1.1.6 (1)", but 1.1.6 lists principles and 1.1.5(1) defines a Takaful Operator; the activity of Takaful Business is defined in GEN Schedule 1, paragraph 25. The meaning survives in each case.

findings.act: AIFC Banking Business Prudential Rules (BBR), V6

en.title: Capital conservation ratios: Table 4A is entered by the CET1 capital ratio, while the buffer under 4.31(2) excludes CET1 used for the T1 and Total Capital ratios
en.summary: BBR 4.31(2) provides that the capital conservation buffer must be made up of CET1 capital above the amounts used to meet the CET1, T1 and Total Capital ratios, and 4.32(1) requires a bank whose buffer falls below the required minimum to restrict its distributions. Under 4.32(2) and Table 4A, however, the minimum capital conservation ratio is selected by the bank's CET1 capital ratio, which does not exclude the CET1 used to meet the T1 and Total Capital ratios; a ratio above 7% gives 0%. For a bank whose capital is all CET1, the buffer becomes positive only above 8% of risk-weighted assets and reaches 2.5% at 10.5%. With risk-weighted assets of USD 1,000 million, CET1 of USD 85 million (8.5%) and no AT1 or T2 capital, the bank's ratios are above the minima, its buffer under 4.31(2) is USD 5 million against USD 25 million, so it is in breach of 4.31(1) and 4.32(1) requires it to restrict distributions; yet Table 4A sets no positive minimum retention (0%). BPG Chapter 4 paragraph 11(c) states that a bank with a CET1 capital ratio of more than 7% can distribute 100% of its earnings; 4.33(1) also compares CET1 with the CET1 ratio plus the buffer. IBB 5.2 to 5.4 and Table 5.1 have the same structure. Basel III paragraph 131 measures the CET1 ratio of the table excluding the CET1 needed for the 6% Tier 1 and 8% Total Capital requirements.
en.correction: Please clarify how the restriction under 4.32(1) is quantified for such a bank, and consider either measuring column 2 of Table 4A as the CET1 capital ratio excluding the CET1 used to meet the T1 and Total Capital ratios (4.5% plus the buffer under 4.31(2)) and aligning 4.33(1), BPG Chapter 4 paragraph 11 and IBB 5.3 to 5.4, or, if Table 4A reflects the intended policy, aligning 4.31(2) and Form 30 line 7 with it.

en.title: Significant and non-significant investments: the definition in 4.27, the heading of 4.29(4) and the conditions of 4.29(4)(a) and 4.29(6)(a) classify a holding of AT1 or T2 instruments differently
en.summary: BBR 4.27 defines a significant investment as an investment of 10% or more in the common shares, or other instruments that qualify as capital, of the entity concerned. The heading of Rule 4.29(4), which is part of the Rules under section 24(1)(a) of the AIFC Regulations on AIFC Acts, describes non-significant investments as those "where the Bank does not own more than 10% of issued common equity of the entity". Rule 4.29(4) then applies where the Bank makes a non-significant investment and does not own more than 10% of the common shares, and Rule 4.29(6) where the Bank makes a significant investment and owns 10% or more of the common shares. A holding of 10% or more of an issue of AT1 or T2 instruments of another bank or insurer, with less than 10% of its common shares, is non-significant by the heading and significant by 4.27, and under the conditions of the two rules it is outside both of them. Take an unconsolidated issuer whose only instrument other than common shares is a T2 issue of USD 300 million, with no reciprocal holding and no pledge: for a bank with CET1 of USD 100 million, a holding of USD 30 million (10% of the issue) with no common shares is not deducted under the conditions of 4.29, while the heading and line 37 of Form 30 lead to a deduction of the excess of USD 20 million; a holding of USD 29.7 million (9.9%) leads to a deduction of USD 19.7 million. The heading also uses "not more than 10%" where 4.27 uses "10% or more".
en.correction: Please consider either testing significance in 4.27 by the holding of common shares only, as the heading of 4.29(4) and line 37 of Form 30 do, and aligning the 10% boundary, or replacing the common-share conditions in the heading and in 4.29(4)(a)(iii) and 4.29(6)(a)(iii) with a reference to a non-significant and a significant investment as defined, so that 4.29(6)(b) applies to such holdings (a full deduction, stricter than testing significance by common shares only).

en.title: Maturity mismatch limits: the net cumulative position is inflows less outflows, and 9.21(4) requires it not to exceed negative 15% and negative 25%
en.summary: BBR 9.21(1)(c) defines the net cumulative maturity mismatch position as inflows (assets) less outflows (liabilities) in each time band, and 9.21(3) expresses it as a percentage of Total Deposits; line 5 of Form 81 in the Manual for Preparation of Returns uses the same sign. Rule 9.21(4) then requires the position not to exceed negative 15% (sight to 8 days) and negative 25% (sight to 1 month), and the Bank must notify the AFSA if it exceeds these limits. Read as written, a bank with Total Deposits of USD 100 million whose inflows up to 8 days are USD 110 million and outflows USD 100 million (a position of +10%) exceeds negative 15% and breaches the limit, while a bank whose inflows are USD 40 million against outflows of USD 100 million (-60%) does not exceed it. The flows are those included in the maturity ladder under the BPG. IBB 10.30(4) and (5) have the same text (the denominator in IBB 10.30(3) also includes UPSIA accounts).
en.correction: Please consider setting negative 15% and negative 25% as lower bounds of the position (keeping the denominators in BBR 9.21(3) and IBB 10.30(3)), and aligning the notification duty so that it applies when the position falls below a bound (the last sentence of BBR 9.21(4) and IBB 10.30(5)).

en.title: NSFR required stable funding: unencumbered HQLA securities with a residual maturity of one year or more fall within the descriptions of two RSF categories
en.summary: Under BPG Chapter 9 paragraph 177(a) each asset is assigned to one of the eight RSF categories, and BBR 9.19(2) requires the NSFR to be calculated in accordance with Chapter 9 of the BPG (it refers to Section E; the NSFR methodology is in Section H). Paragraph 179 assigns unencumbered Level 1 HQLA to Category 2 (5%), paragraphs 181 and 182(a) assign Level 2A and 2B HQLA to Categories 4 and 5 (15% and 50%), and paragraph 184(c) assigns 'unencumbered securities with residual maturity of 1 year or more' to Category 7 (85%). Unlike paragraph 184(d) and row 24 of the disclosure template Table 13, paragraph 184(c) does not exclude securities that qualify as HQLA, and no rule sets which description prevails. For a bank with available stable funding of USD 1,000 million, other required stable funding of USD 700 million and an unencumbered five-year Level 1 government bond of USD 500 million, the NSFR is 137.9% under paragraph 179 and 88.9% under paragraph 184(c). Form 201 in the Manual for Preparation of Returns repeats both lines (10.1 and 15.3), and IBB Appendix 1 paragraphs 131 and 136(c) repeat the same overlap (for an Islamic Bank, for example a Level 1 sovereign sukuk).
en.correction: Please consider assigning HQLA securities to one category unambiguously, for example by excluding securities that qualify as HQLA from BPG Chapter 9 paragraph 184(c), as paragraph 184(d) and Table 13 row 24 do, and from IBB Appendix 1 paragraph 136(c), and aligning Form 201 line 15.3.

en.title: Accumulated losses already reflected in retained earnings: IBB 4.13 and 4.39
en.summary: IBB 4.13(c) includes retained earnings in Common Equity Tier 1 capital, and the Guidance to 4.13, which under IBB 1.3(b) is part of the rules, states that retained earnings and other comprehensive income include appropriated profit or loss. IBB 4.13(f) includes the regulatory adjustments under 4.30, which points to 4.31 to 4.45, and IBB 4.39 requires an Islamic Bank to deduct from its CET1 capital the amount of any accumulated losses, without distinguishing losses already reflected in retained earnings. Read as written, a loss of prior years reduces CET1 capital twice: an Islamic Bank with common shares of USD 100 million and retained earnings of minus USD 20 million would report CET1 of USD 60 million, or USD 80 million if 4.39 does not apply to losses already reflected in retained earnings. BBR 4.14(c) and 4.28(11) have the same structure, and BPG Chapter 4 paragraph 7 states the same for BBR 4.14.
en.correction: Please clarify whether 4.39 is meant to reduce CET1 capital again for losses already reflected in retained earnings; if not, consider stating that it applies only to losses not yet reflected there (for example the loss for the current financial year). The same question applies to BBR 4.28(11).

en.title: Islamic banks — significant and non-significant investments: an investment that is significant under 4.29 through Additional Tier 1 or Tier 2 instruments, with less than 10% of the common shares, is not covered by 4.43 or 4.45
en.summary: IBB 4.29 defines a significant investment as an investment of 10% or more in the common shares, or other instruments that qualify as capital, of the entity concerned. Rule 4.43 applies where the Islamic Bank makes a non-significant investment and does not own 10% or more of the common shares; Rule 4.45 applies where it makes a significant investment and owns 10% or more of the common shares. An investment that is significant through Additional Tier 1 or Tier 2 instruments, with less than 10% of the common shares, is outside both rules, and no other rule in 4.40 to 4.46 deducts it: 4.42 covers reciprocal cross holdings only, and 4.45(3) and 4.46 cover common shares and other CET 1 instruments only. The headings of 4.43 to 4.45 do not refer to the shareholding. Take an unconsolidated Islamic Bank whose only instrument other than common shares is an issue of Tier 2 sukuk of USD 300 million, with no reciprocal holding and no pledge: for an Islamic Bank with CET 1 Capital of USD 100 million, a holding of USD 30 million (10% of the issue) with no common shares is not deducted, while a holding of USD 29.7 million (9.9%) leads to a deduction of the excess of USD 19.7 million under 4.44.
en.correction: Please consider either testing significance in 4.29 by the holding of common shares only and aligning 4.45(1)(c), or replacing the common-share conditions in 4.43(1)(c) and 4.45(1)(c) with a reference to a non-significant and a significant investment as defined, so that 4.45(2) applies to such holdings (a full deduction, stricter than testing significance by common shares only).

en.title: Part 4 covers issuers of Commodity stablecoins, but authorisation (4.1) and capital (4.2) name only Fiat stablecoins
en.summary: Amendments No. 3 (approved 13 April 2025, in force 13 October 2025) extended the Part 4 application statement to "issuing Fiat stablecoins and Commodity stablecoins", but in the same instrument added only "or issuing Fiat stablecoins" to 4.1(1), the lead-in of 4.2 and 4.2(b). The current version keeps this. Rule 4.11.3(1) says "In addition to DAA 4.2(b), an issuer of a Fiat stablecoin or Commodity stablecoin" must hold ongoing capital of 2%, so it assumes that 4.2(b) applies to both. GEN Schedule 1, paragraph 21, Guidance (5) also mentions only Fiat stablecoins. A Commodity-stablecoin issuer might be covered as "Providing Money Services in relation to Digital Assets" (buying and selling of a Digital Asset), but 4.1(2) treats issuing as a separate activity. The rules therefore do not say clearly which licence a Commodity-stablecoin issuer needs or whether the USD 200,000 floor in 4.2(b) applies to it.
en.correction: Please clarify how rules 4.1 and 4.2 apply to issuers of Commodity stablecoins, including the licence category and the minimum capital, for example by adding "or Commodity stablecoins" after "issuing Fiat stablecoins" in 4.1(1), the lead-in of 4.2 and 4.2(b).

en.title: DAA 2.8.2(1)(c): stablecoin admission criteria "in (4) or (5)": (5) is a notice after admission, and the reserve test in (4)(c) covers only Fiat stablecoins
en.summary: DAA 2.8.2(1)(c) makes admission of a Fiat or Commodity stablecoin to trading depend on "all of the requirements in (4) or (5) as applicable". Paragraph (4) lists reserve criteria, but its test of reserve adequacy in (4)(c) speaks only of "reserves in respect of Fiat stablecoins". Paragraph (5) is not a criterion: it requires the operator to notify the AFSA within 3 business days after admission (in earlier versions, 10 days before admission). So for a Commodity stablecoin the operator has no stated test that the reserves cover the stablecoins in circulation. Issuers licensed in the AIFC must still meet the reserve rules in DAA 4.7.1, which cover Commodity stablecoins, and the AFSA approves stablecoins other than those issued by licensed Digital Asset Service Providers (2.8.1(3)(b)); the gap concerns the operator's admission test, mainly for stablecoins issued outside the AIFC. PMS 2.4.2(1)(c) has the same wording (AIFC2-PMS-02).
en.correction: Please state the reserve test that applies when a Commodity stablecoin is admitted to trading, and in 2.8.2(1)(c) refer only to the paragraphs that contain admission criteria.

en.title: DAA 4.11.3: is the base of the 2% ongoing capital the outstanding stablecoins or the reserve assets?
en.summary: DAA 4.11.3(1) sets ongoing capital at 2% "of the average outstanding Fiat stablecoins or Commodity stablecoins". For an issuer with several categories, 4.11.3(3) says this amount "should be the sum of the average amounts of the reserve assets backing each category", and the Guidance describes it as the average amount of reserve assets at the end of each day over the preceding 6 months. Reserve assets must be at least equal to the outstanding stablecoins (4.7.1(2)) and may be larger. For an issuer with one category, the binding text does not say which base applies or over what period the average is taken.
en.correction: Please state in the rule whether the base is outstanding stablecoins or reserve assets, and move the averaging period into the rule.

en.title: PMS 4.3 and 7.3(3) list different cases in which a redemption fee may be charged: may a fee be charged for a redemption during the agreement?
en.summary: Two rules govern fees on the redemption of Electronic Money, and both use "only where". PMS 4.3(1) allows a fee where (a) the redemption is requested before the termination of the client agreement, (b) a fixed-term agreement is terminated early, or (c) redemption is requested more than one year after termination. PMS 7.3(3) allows a fee only where it "relates to early termination or late redemption". A redemption requested at early termination meets both rules. A redemption during a running agreement, without termination, is allowed by 4.3(1)(a) and referred to in 4.4(1), but does not fit 7.3(3). Read together, such a fee is not allowed, which leaves little room for 4.3(1)(a).
en.correction: Please clarify whether a fee may be charged for a redemption, including a partial redemption, during a running agreement, and align rules 4.3 and 7.3(3).

en.title: PMS 2.4.2(1)(c): stablecoin criteria "in subrules (4) or (5)": (5) is a prior notice, and the reserve test in (4)(c) covers only Fiat stablecoins
en.summary: PMS 2.4.2(1)(c) requires, for a Fiat or Commodity stablecoin, that "all of the requirements in subrules (4) or (5) as applicable are met". Subrule (4) gives reserve criteria, but its reserve-adequacy test in (4)(c) speaks only of "reserves in respect of Fiat stablecoins". Subrule (5) requires the provider to notify the AFSA at least 10 days before admission; it can be read as a condition of admission, but the text does not say when (5) applies instead of (4). No reserve-adequacy test is stated for Commodity stablecoins. DAA 2.8.2(1)(c) has the same wording (AIFC2-DAA-04).
en.correction: Please clarify when subrule (5) applies instead of subrule (4), and state the reserve test for Commodity stablecoins.

en.title: DAA 4.7: the reserve of a Fiat stablecoin is only operationally segregated; the Rules do not say whether it is protected from the issuer's own creditors and how it is shared among holders on insolvency
en.summary: DAA 4.7.1(4) requires the issuer of a Fiat stablecoin to ensure that the reserve of assets is "operationally segregated from the proprietary assets of the issuer". DAA 4.7.3(7) requires the custody arrangements to protect the reserve against "claims of the custodian's creditors", and DAA 4.7.3(1)(a) requires that the reserve is "not encumbered nor pledged as Collateral". DAA 4.11.2(1) requires the issuer to grant holders redemption rights "on the reserve assets when the issuer is not able to comply with its obligations", while DAA 4.5(1)(c) speaks of "the rights or the absence of rights granted to the holders". The DAA, PMS and COB do not state that the reserve is held on trust for holders or is otherwise outside the issuer's estate. Under the Insolvency Regulations (Schedule 3) property of a company excludes only property held on trust, and under rule 5.46.1 of the Insolvency Rules unsecured debts rank equally. Because the issuer is a Money Service Provider (DAA 4.1(1)), COB 8.2 applies to it (COB 8.1.4), and COB 8.2.16(2)(c) requires money remaining with the firm to be paid to each Client before the general order of winding up; it is not clear whether this covers the reserve, which is not Client Money under COB 8.2.1 and PMS 9.3, and holders who have no client agreement with the issuer (DAA 4.11.2(3)). DAA 4.7.2(3)(b) refers to an issuer "required to implement a redemption plan", but no rule sets out such a plan. Example: if the reserve forms part of the estate and holders rank as unsecured creditors, an issuer with 50 million USD of coins in circulation, a reserve of 50 million USD, no other assets, other unsecured creditors of 10 million USD and winding-up costs of 1 million USD pays holders about 82 cents per coin (49 / 60). The wording of 4.7.1(4), 4.7.3(7) and 4.11.2(1) is close to Articles 36(3), 37 and 39(1) of the EU Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (EU) 2023/1114; Article 36(2) of that Regulation, which requires the reserve to be legally segregated from the issuer's estate so that the issuer's creditors have no recourse to it, has no counterpart in the DAA.
en.correction: Please clarify whether the reserve of assets is legally segregated from the issuer's estate and how it is distributed among holders if the issuer becomes insolvent, including how DAA 4.11.2 relates to COB 8.2.16. If protection is intended, the DAA could provide that the reserve is held on trust for holders and set out the order of distribution and a redemption plan.

en.title: Unclear application of the Client Money Rules to fiat currency held for Clients in Digital Asset Business
en.summary: The Glossary defines Investment Business as a list of activities (a) to (k), "but not including Digital Asset Business", and Digital Asset Business includes Operating a Digital Asset Trading Facility and the other activities in relation to Digital Assets. COB 8.1.4 requires compliance with the Client Money Rules (COB 8.2) by a firm that holds Money for a Client "in the course of, or in connection with, the carrying on of Investment Business or Provides Money Services", and COB 8.2.1 defines Client Money by Investment Business. A Digital Asset Trading Facility Operator holds fiat currency for its Clients (DAA 2.13.4(2): a trade only if there are "sufficient Fiat Currencies or Digital Assets … in the Client's account"). Digital Assets of the same Clients "must be held on trust" (DAA 2.13.7(2), 3.7.1(3)), but no rule says the same of their fiat currency. The Rules of cooperation with second-tier banks require a Digital Asset Service Provider to hold Clients' money and its own money in separate accounts (rule 2.2.3), and DAA 2.13.7(7)(a) requires "segregation and portability arrangements". COB chapter 8 is listed among the applicable provisions only in Guidance to DAA chapters 2 and 3. It is therefore unclear whether this fiat currency is Client Money, whether the Client Money Distribution Rules in COB 8.2.16 apply to it if the firm fails (COB 8.1.2(c) brings in chapter 8 for a firm that Provides Custody, but not for a trading facility that uses a third-party wallet provider or for a broker), and whether it is Excluded Property under Schedule 4 of the Insolvency Rules. Example: a client deposits 20,000 USD with a Digital Asset Trading Facility Operator that uses a third-party wallet provider; the money is held in a separate account under rule 2.2.3; if the operator fails with a shortfall in that account, the Rules do not say how the shortfall is shared.
en.correction: Please clarify whether fiat currency held for Clients by Digital Asset Service Providers is Client Money, and if it is meant to be, apply the Client Money Rules to it, for example by a rule in the DAA or by adjusting the exclusion of Digital Asset Business for the purposes of COB 8.

en.title: Capital of Digital Asset Service Providers: DAA Table 2 and PRU (INV) Table 3.3 both apply to the same activities with different amounts
en.summary: DAA 3.2(1)(b) and Table 2 set the capital of a Digital Asset Service Provider at USD 250,000 for Providing Custody, USD 100,000 for Managing Investments and USD 250,000 for Dealing in Investments as Principal (other than matched principal). PRU (INV) 1.3 applies to any firm authorised to conduct these activities; Investments include Digital Assets (Glossary), and PRU (INV) 1.3(6) does not exclude Digital Asset Business. PRU (INV) Table 3.3 sets USD 500,000 for Providing Custody Services and for Dealing in Investments as Principal and USD 150,000 for Managing Investments, with the liquid assets requirement in PRU (INV) 4. DAA 3.2(1)(a) keeps the general authorisation requirements of other applicable rules, and for stablecoin issuers DAA 4.2(b) states that "the highest amount applies" where another activity requires more capital, so the DAA amounts may be meant as a floor next to PRU (INV). The Rules do not say so for Table 2. Example: a firm licensed only to provide custody of Digital Assets with capital resources of USD 300,000 meets Table 2, but is USD 200,000 below PRU (INV) Table 3.3 for the same activity.
en.correction: Please state whether the DAA Table 2 amounts are meant to replace or to supplement PRU (INV) for Digital Asset Service Providers. If they replace it, PRU (INV) 1.3 could exclude Digital Asset Business; if PRU (INV) applies, Table 2 could say that the higher amount applies.

en.title: Companies Regulations s.92: the consolidated PDFs on aifc.kz make the fine clause refer to itself; Amendments No. 2 and the AFSA online text number it correctly
en.summary: In Amendments No. 2 to the Companies Regulations (in force 1 March 2019) section 92 has subsections (3) on the periods of a disqualification order, (4) "A Person must not Contravene an order under subsection (2)" and (5) "Contravention of subsection (4) is punishable by a fine." The consolidated PDF versions on aifc.kz from V3 to the current V8 drop the number (3). The text of (3) runs on as part of (2), the prohibition becomes (3), and the fine clause, now numbered (4), reads "Contravention of subsection (4)", so in these PDFs it refers to itself. The Companies Regulations on the AFSA website (read on 24 October 2026) keep the numbering (3), (4) and (5) as adopted, so the problem is limited to the aifc.kz PDFs.
en.correction: Please restore the numbering (3), (4) and (5) of section 92, as adopted by Amendments No. 2, in the consolidated PDF on aifc.kz.

en.title: Companies Regulations s.26-1(2)(b): the confirmation statement covers duties "mentioned in subsection (2)", but the duties are listed in (3)

en.title: Companies Regulations s.26(4): the fine clause was not updated when Amendments No. 4 moved the annual-return deadline and contents into a new subsection (1-1)
en.summary: Amendments No. 4 moved the annual-return deadline and contents from section 26(1) of the Companies Regulations into a new subsection (1-1). Section 26(4) still makes "subsection (1), (2-1) or (3)" punishable by a fine, and item 10 of Schedule 3 of the Companies Rules still says "26(1) or (3)". The reference to (1) may be read as reaching the re-enacted duty (section 21(2) of the AIFC Regulations on AIFC Acts), but a reader of section 26(4) cannot see that late or incomplete filing is finable. Item 10 also does not list subsection (2-1), which section 26(4) makes finable.
en.correction: Please consider amending section 26(4) to read "subsection (1), (1-1), (2-1) or (3)", and please align item 10 of Schedule 3 of the Companies Rules, which also omits (2-1).

en.title: Companies Rules 5.3 (transfer out of the AIFC): since V4 the subrules are numbered 5.3.3-5.3.6, and three cross-references, including the 60-day notice, point to numbers that no longer exist

en.title: Insolvency Regulations ss.98-99: where inability to pay is proved to the Court, which date is the "onset of Insolvency"?
en.summary: Sections 98 and 99 of the Insolvency Regulations measure look-back periods to "the onset of Insolvency". For Part 10, Schedule 3 defines "Insolvency" as being Unable to Pay its Debts, the approval of a Voluntary Arrangement or the appointment of a Receiver or Administrative Receiver. Where inability to pay is "proved to the satisfaction of the Court" (section 50(1)(c) and (2)), the text does not say whether the onset is the date the inability began or the date of the Court's finding; section 98(c) points to the order date for one case only. For comparison, the corresponding ADGM provision (Insolvency Regulations 2015, section 259(3)) defines the onset of insolvency in a separate subsection by reference to formal events.
en.correction: Please clarify, for the section 50(1)(c) and (2) cases, which date is the onset of Insolvency for sections 98 and 99.
