findings.act: Programmablaufplan for wage-tax withholding 2026 (§ 39b(6) EStG) and Income Tax Act (EStG)
findings.location: Wage-tax program 2026, method MZTABFB; § 9a sentence 2 EStG

en.title: Wage-tax program 2026 caps the employee lump-sum allowance after deducting the old-age relief and the tax-card allowance; § 9a EStG caps it at income
en.summary: § 9a sentence 2 EStG allows the employee lump-sum allowance only up to the amount of income. The program caps it at the wage left after the old-age relief amount and any allowance on the tax card have been deducted, so these amounts can be lost. We ran the official XML and a reading of the statutory text on the same inputs. The Federal Ministry of Finance points to the order of deductions in § 39b(2) EStG; that order is not in dispute, and the provision does not state the size of the cap. The program does not declare a deviation under § 39b(6) sentence 2. The text does not expressly say how the cap works in withholding, so this record reports a discrepancy and not a breach of the law.
en.impact: Example: a company pension of 20,000 euros plus 1,000 euros of active wages from the same employer, tax class I, age 64: 506 euros of wage tax under the program and 475 euros under the reading of the text. An approximate income tax assessment with the same contribution allowance also gives 475 euros. With an allowance of 1,140 euros for a disability, the calculated difference is 184 euros. The difference can be recovered through an assessment, which is not mandatory for everyone. With an add-back amount on the tax card the difference runs the other way, by 47 to 48 euros in our cases.
en.correction: Cap the allowance at wages excluding pension payments, before these deductions, or declare the step as a deviation under § 39b(6) sentence 2 with its grounds, or clarify § 9a sentence 2 for withholding.

quote_translations.norm: the lump sums under sentence 1 number 1 letter a and number 3 may be deducted only up to the amount of the income.

de.title: PAP 2026 begrenzt den Arbeitnehmer-Pauschbetrag nach Abzug von Altersentlastungsbetrag und Freibetrag; § 9a EStG begrenzt ihn auf die Einnahmen
de.summary: § 9a Satz 2 EStG lässt den Arbeitnehmer-Pauschbetrag nur bis zur Höhe der Einnahmen zu. Der PAP begrenzt ihn auf den Arbeitslohn nach Abzug von Altersentlastungsbetrag und Freibetrag, sodass diese Beträge verloren gehen können. Das amtliche XML und eine Lesart des Wortlauts wurden mit denselben Eingaben ausgeführt. Das BMF verweist auf die Reihenfolge des Abzugs nach § 39b Abs. 2 EStG; diese Reihenfolge ist nicht streitig, und die Vorschrift nennt die Höhe der Grenze nicht. Der PAP weist keine Abweichung nach § 39b Abs. 6 Satz 2 aus. Wie die Grenze im Lohnsteuerabzug wirkt, sagt der Wortlaut nicht ausdrücklich; dieser Eintrag beschreibt daher eine Abweichung und keinen Gesetzesverstoß.
de.impact: Beispiel: Werkspension 20 000 € und aktiver Arbeitslohn 1 000 € beim selben Arbeitgeber, Steuerklasse I, 64 Jahre: Lohnsteuer 506 € nach PAP, 475 € nach der Lesart des Wortlauts. Eine überschlägige Veranlagung mit derselben Vorsorgepauschale ergibt ebenfalls 475 €. Mit einem Freibetrag von 1 140 € wegen Behinderung beträgt der berechnete Unterschied 184 €. Der Unterschied lässt sich in der Veranlagung ausgleichen, die nicht für alle verpflichtend ist. Bei einem Hinzurechnungsbetrag verläuft er in unseren Fällen umgekehrt, um 47 bis 48 €.
de.correction: Begrenzung auf den Arbeitslohn ohne Versorgungsbezüge vor diesen Abzügen, oder Ausweis als Abweichung nach § 39b Abs. 6 Satz 2 mit Begründung, oder Klarstellung von § 9a Satz 2 für den Lohnsteuerabzug.

Income Tax Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.)), s. 122.5
findings.location: Result for a pay dated 1 January or 1 July, when a new T4127 edition takes effect

en.title: PDOC: when a new edition starts, time zones east of Eastern time get the amounts of the previous day
en.summary: PDOC says that the date the employee is paid decides the tax rates and the CPP and EI figures, and that the July 2026 changes apply to a date paid of July 1, 2026 or later. On 23 October 2026 we ran the public calculator many times with the same entries and changed only the time zone of the browser (automated Google Chrome 155). On the day each new edition we tried took effect (1 July 2025, 1 January 2026 and 1 July 2026) the result screen showed the selected date, but in Atlantic (Halifax) and Newfoundland (St. John's) time PDOC used the amounts of the previous day. Labrador time (Goose Bay), tried on 1 July 2026, behaved the same. Toronto and Vancouver time got the new amounts. The days before and after gave the same result in every time zone. Examples, monthly pay of 4,000.00 CAD: British Columbia, 1 July 2026: provincial tax 132.21 CAD instead of 160.43 CAD. Ontario, 1 January 2026, TD1 amounts as PDOC fills them in: PDOC filled in the 2025 amounts (16,129 and 12,747 instead of 16,452 and 12,989) and showed federal tax 314.59 instead of 310.53, provincial tax 171.40 instead of 170.40 and EI 65.60 instead of 65.20. Newfoundland and Labrador, 1 July 2026: PDOC filled in 11,188 instead of 15,000 as the provincial TD1 amount (provincial tax 255.95 instead of 228.31). The PDF of the result made in Halifax time shows a date one day earlier than the screen. The form sends the date as the local midnight of the computer; we cannot see the server, so we do not know the cause. We did not check what employers actually withheld.
en.impact: A payroll operator in these time zones who enters a pay date of 1 January or 1 July sees the amounts of the previous day under the selected date. Example: provincial tax of 132.21 CAD instead of 160.43 CAD for a monthly pay of 4,000.00 CAD in British Columbia on 1 July 2026.
en.correction: One selected date should give one set of rates and amounts, the same pre-filled TD1 amounts and the same date in the PDF, whatever the time zone of the computer.

en.title: Schedule 8 (2025) e-text: line 75 has no percent sign
en.summary: In the accessible e-text of Schedule 8 for 2025, Part 5, line 75 says "multiply by 83.1933 =". The PDF of the same form, the read-aloud text of the PDF and line 9 of the e-text all have "83.1933%". Read as printed, line 75 would be 100 times too large. It cancels out by line 88, so the final amounts do not change. In the same e-text, page 1 says "Page 1 of 10" (the other pages say "of 11"), and the opening instruction on page 6 is labelled "Line 36", where the PDF has line 37.
en.impact: No final amount changes. A reader who works through the e-text by hand or with a screen reader gets different intermediate lines: with an amount of 100.00, line 75 is 8,319.33 in the e-text and 83.19 in the PDF.
en.correction: Line 75: "multiplied by 83.1933% =", as on line 9. Page 1: "Page 1 of 11". Page 6: "Line 37".

en.title: T4127 (123rd edition), Option 2, Prince Edward Island: "Form TD1NL" instead of "Form TD1PE"

en.title: § 63(2) EStG refers to sentence 3 of subsection (1); the children it means have been in sentence 6 since 2014
en.summary: Subsection (2) empowers the Federal Government to provide child benefit for “children described in subsection 1 sentence 3, first half-sentence”. It means children living outside Germany, the EU and the EEA. The act of 2 December 2014 inserted three sentences into subsection (1) and itself calls the sentence on those children the “new sentence 6”. Sentence 3 now deals with the identification number and has no half-sentences. Subsection (2) was not changed.
en.impact: The power to issue the ordinance points to a sentence that does not describe any such children. Effects on an ordinance or on individual cases have not been examined.
en.correction: Replace “Absatz 1 Satz 3 erster Halbsatz” with “Absatz 1 Satz 6 erster Halbsatz”.

de.title: § 63 Abs. 2 EStG verweist auf Absatz 1 Satz 3; die gemeinten Kinder stehen seit 2014 in Satz 6
de.summary: Absatz 2 ermächtigt die Bundesregierung zu Regelungen für die „in Absatz 1 Satz 3 erster Halbsatz bezeichneten Kinder“. Gemeint sind Kinder ohne Wohnsitz oder gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt im Inland, in der EU oder im EWR. Das Gesetz vom 2. Dezember 2014 fügte in Absatz 1 drei Sätze ein und spricht selbst vom „neuen Satz 6“. Satz 3 regelt seitdem die Identifikationsnummer und hat keinen Halbsatz. Absatz 2 blieb unverändert.
de.impact: Die Ermächtigung verweist auf einen Satz, der solche Kinder nicht beschreibt. Auswirkungen auf eine Verordnung oder auf Einzelfälle sind nicht untersucht.
de.correction: „Absatz 1 Satz 3 erster Halbsatz“ durch „Absatz 1 Satz 6 erster Halbsatz“ ersetzen.

en.title: § 41b(4) EStG assigns competence for subsection (2a), which was repealed in 2019
en.summary: Sentence 1 of subsection (4) makes the employer's local tax office competent also “for the application of subsection 2a”. Article 74 No. 7(b) of the act of 20 November 2019 repealed subsection (2a) and did not change subsection (4). The current text shows subsection (2a) as “weggefallen”. Article 5 No. 1 of the draft Annual Tax Act 2026 amends § 41b and leaves subsection (4) as it is.
en.impact: The competence rule names a provision that no longer exists. No incorrect application has been shown.
en.correction: Delete “sowie für die Anwendung des Absatzes 2a”.

de.title: § 41b Abs. 4 EStG regelt die Zuständigkeit für den 2019 aufgehobenen Absatz 2a
de.summary: Nach Absatz 4 Satz 1 ist das Betriebsstättenfinanzamt auch „für die Anwendung des Absatzes 2a“ zuständig. Art. 74 Nr. 7 Buchst. b des Gesetzes vom 20. November 2019 hob Absatz 2a auf und ließ Absatz 4 unverändert. Der geltende Text weist Absatz 2a als „weggefallen“ aus. Art. 5 Nr. 1 des Entwurfs des Jahressteuergesetzes 2026 ändert § 41b, lässt Absatz 4 aber unberührt.
de.impact: Die Zuständigkeitsnorm nennt eine Vorschrift, die es nicht mehr gibt. Eine fehlerhafte Anwendung ist nicht gezeigt.
de.correction: Die Wörter „sowie für die Anwendung des Absatzes 2a“ streichen.

en.title: § 34a(11) EStG refers to a separate determination of a term that the Act does not define or regulate
en.summary: Sentence 3 ties the end of the determination period to the tax year at whose end “the amount subject to subsequent taxation and the nachversteuerungsfreies Entnahmevolumen” of the business are to be separately determined. The second term occurs nowhere else in the Act. § 34a does not define it and provides for no determination of such an amount. The wording appears in Bundesgesetzblatt 2024 I No. 108, Art. 3 No. 6. It is absent from the 2009 consolidation and from the act in Bundesgesetzblatt 2016 I p. 1679; the act that introduced it has not been identified.
en.impact: The period rule presupposes a determination for which the Act gives no rule. Effects on the period have not been shown.
en.correction: For the legislator: delete the words if they have no content of their own, or else define the term and regulate its determination.

de.title: § 34a Abs. 11 EStG setzt die Feststellung eines Begriffs voraus, den das Gesetz weder definiert noch regelt
de.summary: Satz 3 knüpft das Ende der Feststellungsfrist an den Veranlagungszeitraum, auf dessen Schluss „der nachversteuerungspflichtige Betrag und das nachversteuerungsfreie Entnahmevolumen“ gesondert festzustellen sind. Der zweite Begriff kommt im EStG sonst nicht vor. § 34a definiert ihn nicht und regelt keine Feststellung eines solchen Betrags. Der Wortlaut steht in BGBl. 2024 I Nr. 108, Art. 3 Nr. 6. In der Neufassung 2009 und in BGBl. 2016 I S. 1679 fehlt er; das einführende Gesetz ist nicht ermittelt.
de.impact: Die Fristregel setzt eine Feststellung voraus, für die das Gesetz keine Regelung enthält. Auswirkungen auf die Frist sind nicht gezeigt.
de.correction: Für den Gesetzgeber: die Wörter streichen, falls sie keinen eigenen Inhalt haben, andernfalls den Begriff und seine Feststellung regeln.

findings.location: Wage-tax program 2026, method STSMIN; § 19a(1) sentence 6 and § 39b(3) sentence 8 EStG

en.title: Wage-tax program 2026: on what basis is a negative difference from a deferred share benefit set off against the month’s wage tax?
en.summary: When a share benefit under § 19a EStG is not yet taxed, it still enters the contribution allowance. That can make the difference under § 39b(3) sentence 8 EStG negative. The program sets this negative amount off against the current month’s wage tax (method STSMIN). The statute does not say how a negative difference is treated. The set-off appears reasonable where contributions on the benefit are deductible on assessment; the program does not state its basis.
en.impact: In favour of the employee, in the month of the transfer. Example: monthly wage 3,000 euros, benefit 2,000 euros: 191 euros of wage tax under the program and 298 euros if the negative difference counts as zero. That zero is also an assumption.
en.correction: State the basis of the set-off in the program, or clarify it in § 19a(1) sentence 6 or § 39b(3) EStG.

de.title: PAP 2026: Auf welcher Grundlage wird ein negativer Unterschiedsbetrag aus einem nach § 19a EStG nicht besteuerten Vorteil mit der Lohnsteuer des Monats verrechnet?
de.summary: Ein nach § 19a EStG vorläufig nicht besteuerter Vorteil wird in die Vorsorgepauschale einbezogen. Dadurch kann der Unterschiedsbetrag nach § 39b Abs. 3 Satz 8 EStG negativ werden. Der PAP verrechnet ihn mit der laufenden Lohnsteuer des Monats (STSMIN). Das Gesetz regelt nicht, wie ein negativer Unterschiedsbetrag zu behandeln ist. Die Verrechnung erscheint sachgerecht, soweit auf den Vorteil Beiträge entfallen, die bei der Veranlagung abziehbar sind; ihre Grundlage nennt der PAP nicht.
de.impact: Zugunsten des Arbeitnehmers, im Monat der Übertragung. Beispiel: Monatslohn 3.000 €, Vorteil 2.000 €: 191 € Lohnsteuer nach PAP, 298 €, wenn der negative Betrag mit null angesetzt wird. Auch dieser Ansatz ist eine Annahme.
de.correction: Die Grundlage der Verrechnung im PAP nennen oder in § 19a Abs. 1 Satz 6 oder § 39b Abs. 3 EStG klarstellen.

findings.location: Wage-tax program 2026, method MRE4; § 19(2) sentence 4 EStG

en.title: Wage-tax program 2026 applies the months of pension to the base of the pension allowance; § 19 EStG says twelve times the initial full month
en.summary: § 19(2) sentence 4 EStG sets the base of the pension allowance at twelve times the pension for the initial full month, plus expected special payments. For part-year pensions a later sentence reduces the allowance by one twelfth per month without a pension. For annual pay periods the program instead multiplies the monthly pension by the number of pension months, and the special payment enters in full. The draft for 2027 is unchanged.
en.impact: Example: pension of 400 euros for 5 months, special payment of 1,000 euros, other wages of 30,000 euros, tax class I: allowance of 384 euros and tax of 2,765 euros under the program; 309.33 euros and 2,784 euros under the reading of the text. The program gives 19 euros less, in favour of the employee.
en.correction: State whether the reduction applies to the base or to the allowance, in the statute or in an explanation in the program.

de.title: PAP 2026 setzt für die Bemessungsgrundlage des Versorgungsfreibetrags die Bezugsmonate an; § 19 EStG nennt das Zwölffache des ersten vollen Monats
de.summary: § 19 Abs. 2 Satz 4 EStG bestimmt als Bemessungsgrundlage das Zwölffache des Versorgungsbezugs für den ersten vollen Monat zuzüglich voraussichtlicher Sonderzahlungen; bei Bezug nur für einen Teil des Jahres ermäßigt sich der Freibetrag um ein Zwölftel je Monat. Der PAP multipliziert bei jährlichem Lohnzahlungszeitraum den Monatsbezug mit der Zahl der Bezugsmonate, die Sonderzahlung geht ungekürzt ein. Der Entwurf 2027 ist unverändert.
de.impact: Beispiel: Versorgungsbezug 400 € für 5 Monate, Sonderzahlung 1.000 €, übriger Arbeitslohn 30.000 €, Steuerklasse I: Freibetrag 384 € und Steuer 2.765 € nach PAP; 309,33 € und 2.784 € nach der Wortlaut-Lesart. Der PAP ergibt 19 € weniger, zugunsten des Arbeitnehmers.
de.correction: Klarstellen, ob die Zwölftelung bei der Bemessungsgrundlage oder beim Freibetrag ansetzt, im Gesetz oder durch eine Erläuterung im PAP.

findings.location: Wage-tax program 2026, methods MST5_6, UPEVP, MBERECH, MRE4

en.title: Wage-tax program 2026 rounds amounts for which the statute names no rounding
en.summary: In tax classes V and VI the program rounds the minimum tax and each bracket amount down to whole euros. It also rounds parts of the contribution allowance, the factor-method tax and the pension allowances. The statute names no rounding for these amounts, and the program does not explain them as deviations under § 39b(6) sentence 2 EStG. The draft for 2027 is unchanged and adds one more rounded bracket.
en.impact: In classes V and VI, 154 of the 172 official test-table values differ from the reading of the text: 126 by under 1 euro and 28 by 1 to 2.07 euros a year. In classes I to IV all 344 values match. Payroll tax is credited on assessment, so the effect is small.
en.correction: Document the rounding rules in full in the program and name the basis for those that deviate from the text.

de.title: PAP 2026 rundet Beträge, für die das Gesetz keine Rundung nennt
de.summary: In den Steuerklassen V und VI rundet der PAP die Mindeststeuer und jeden Stufenbetrag auf volle Euro ab. Gerundet werden auch Teile der Vorsorgepauschale, die Steuer im Faktorverfahren und Versorgungsfreibeträge. Das Gesetz nennt für diese Beträge keine Rundung, und der PAP erläutert sie nicht als Abweichungen nach § 39b Abs. 6 Satz 2 EStG. Der Entwurf 2027 ist unverändert und enthält eine weitere gerundete Stufe.
de.impact: In den Klassen V und VI weichen 154 der 172 amtlichen Prüftabellenwerte von der Wortlaut-Lesart ab: 126 um weniger als 1 €, 28 um 1 € bis 2,07 € im Jahr. In den Klassen I bis IV stimmen alle 344 Werte überein. Die Lohnsteuer wird bei der Veranlagung angerechnet; die Wirkung ist gering.
de.correction: Die Rundungsregeln im PAP vollständig dokumentieren und für Abweichungen vom Wortlaut die Grundlage nennen.

findings.location: Wage-tax program 2026, method MSOLZ; § 4 of the Solidarity Surcharge Act

en.title: Wage-tax program 2026 drops fractions of a cent at a different step of the solidarity surcharge than the reading of the statute
en.summary: The program computes the surcharge from the annual base and then divides it by pay period. The reading of §§ 3 and 4 of the Solidarity Surcharge Act uses the base of the pay period, already cut to whole cents. The two routes are equal except at the step where fractions of a cent are dropped.
en.impact: Example: monthly wage of 7,777.66 euros, class I: 3.54 euros under the program and 3.53 euros under the reading of the text. Six chosen cases each show 1 cent. They say nothing about how often this occurs in practice.
en.correction: Align the rounding step of the statute and the program.

de.title: PAP 2026 lässt beim Solidaritätszuschlag Bruchteile eines Cents auf einer anderen Stufe außer Ansatz als die Wortlaut-Lesart
de.summary: Der PAP berechnet den Zuschlag aus der Jahresbemessungsgrundlage und verteilt ihn dann auf den Lohnzahlungszeitraum. Die Lesart der §§ 3 und 4 SolZG verwendet die bereits auf Cent gekürzte Bemessungsgrundlage des Zeitraums. Beide Wege sind bis auf die Stufe gleich, auf der Bruchteile eines Cents entfallen.
de.impact: Beispiel: Monatslohn 7.777,66 €, Steuerklasse I: 3,54 € nach PAP, 3,53 € nach der Wortlaut-Lesart. Sechs gezielt gewählte Fälle zeigen je 1 Cent. Über die Häufigkeit in der Praxis sagen sie nichts.
de.correction: Die Rundungsstufe in Gesetz und PAP abstimmen.

en.title: Should the wage-tax program describe the Aktivrente exemption that is applied before it runs?
en.summary: Since 1 January 2026, § 3 No. 21 EStG exempts wages of up to 24,000 euros a year for people working past the standard retirement age. Under the ministry’s FAQ the employer deducts the exempt part before applying the program. The draft program for 2027 has no input for this and does not mention it.
en.impact: No incorrect tax has been shown. The relief is about 890 million euros a year for about 168,000 people according to Bundestag paper 21/2673. If payroll programs treated it differently, the results would differ; we have not measured that.
en.correction: Describe the preprocessing in the program with test cases, or add an input. The ministry considers the FAQ sufficient.

de.title: Sollte der PAP die vorab anzuwendende Aktivrente beschreiben?
de.summary: Seit dem 1. Januar 2026 stellt § 3 Nr. 21 EStG Arbeitslohn bis 24.000 € im Jahr für Beschäftigte nach Erreichen der Regelaltersgrenze steuerfrei. Nach den FAQ des BMF mindert der Arbeitgeber den Arbeitslohn vor Anwendung des PAP. Der Entwurf des PAP 2027 enthält dafür weder einen Eingangsparameter noch einen Hinweis.
de.impact: Eine falsche Steuer ist nicht gezeigt. Die Entlastung beträgt nach BT-Drs. 21/2673 rund 890 Mio. € im Jahr für rund 168.000 Personen. Würden Programme sie unterschiedlich behandeln, wichen die Ergebnisse voneinander ab; gemessen ist das nicht.
de.correction: Die Vorverarbeitung im PAP mit Prüffällen beschreiben oder einen Eingangsparameter vorsehen. Das BMF hält die FAQ für ausreichend.

findings.location: Gloas fork logic (upgrade) and beacon chain (slot processing, attestation flags)

en.title: Gloas: the payload availability bit of the fork slot is never cleared
en.summary: The Gloas upgrade sets every bit of the payload availability vector to 1. After that, the processing of each slot clears the bit of the next slot. The bit of the fork slot would be cleared while the last Fulu slot is processed, but that slot runs under the Fulu rules, before the upgrade, so the bit stays 1 even when the payload of the fork block is never revealed. Attestation rewards read this bit to decide whether a vote matches the payload status. The case differs from issue 5661, where the last Fulu slot is empty and the bit belongs to a Fulu slot.
en.impact: Minimal preset, fork at slot 16: block 16 is applied and its payload is withheld, slot 17 is empty, and block 18 builds on block 16 without its payload. Honest attesters of slot 17 who saw no payload vote index 0 and get the timely head flag in 0 of 4 cases; attesters who vote index 1 get it in 4 of 4. The same shape at slot 20 gives the reverse result, 4 of 4 for index 0.
en.correction: Clear the bit of the fork slot in the Gloas upgrade function. The bits of the Fulu slots stay 1, because Fulu blocks carry their payload. With this one-line change the fork slot gives the same result as slot 20.

findings.location: Gloas fork choice, honest validator guide and networking (bid gossip)

en.title: Gloas fork choice and honest validator rules do not cover Fulu blocks and Fulu store entries at the fork
en.summary: Issue 5096 and the open pull request 5125 cover one place where Gloas fork choice reads the bid field of a Fulu parent block. The text has further places of this kind. The finalized and safe execution block hashes for the execution layer are read from the bid field of blocks that stay Fulu blocks for at least two epochs after the fork. Bid gossip ignores every bid for the fork slot, because only envelopes fill the list of known payloads and the last Fulu payload never arrives in an envelope. Fork choice gives a Fulu head only an EMPTY child, since a Fulu block never has an envelope, so the honest validator guide tells the proposer of the initial Gloas block to use the parent hash of the last Fulu payload, while the state transition requires the hash of that payload itself. The fork-choice store has no conversion at the fork, although the types of block timeliness and latest messages change in Gloas.
en.impact: Minimal preset, fork at epoch 2: the initial Gloas block built with the parent block hash from the EMPTY branch of the validator guide is invalid; the same block built with the FULL branch is valid. The fork-choice half is shown by the text, not by execution.
en.correction: Add a short fork transition section to the fork-choice text: how existing store entries are converted, whether a Fulu block counts as FULL in Gloas fork choice (or a pre-Gloas exception in the validator guide), and one helper that returns the execution block hash of a block of either fork.

findings.location: Gloas honest builder guide (bid signature) against the beacon chain (bid verification)

en.title: Gloas: a builder bid for the fork slot is signed with the Fulu fork version and fails verification
en.summary: The honest builder guide signs a bid with the domain of the state the builder works with, and the steps before it take that state from the head of the chain. For a bid for the fork slot the head is the last Fulu block, so the domain uses the Fulu fork version, although the epoch passed in is the Gloas fork epoch. The block that includes the bid is processed on the upgraded state, where verification uses the Gloas fork version, so the signature does not verify and the block is rejected. Proposer preferences (issues 5656 and 5665) and inclusion lists (pull request 5721) had the same problem and were fixed by taking the version from the epoch; bids were not changed. Bid gossip also ignores bids for the fork slot today (issue 5795), so the problem shows once that is fixed, or for bids that reach the proposer another way.
en.impact: Minimal preset, fork at epoch 2: the same bid for the fork slot, verified on the upgraded state, is invalid when signed with the head state and valid when signed with the upgraded state.
en.correction: Compute the domain from the fork version of the epoch of the bid, as was done for proposer preferences.

findings.location: Gloas and Fulu networking: executable gossip checks

en.title: Executable gossip checks take the signature domain from the head state, so the opening block of a fork fails the proposer signature check
en.summary: The executable block gossip check in Gloas takes the state of the current head and computes the proposer signature domain from it. When the opening block of a fork arrives, the head is still the last block of the previous fork, and the domain takes the previous fork version from that state. A valid signature does not verify, and the block is rejected as having an invalid proposer signature. The same pattern is in the Gloas checks for aggregates, payload attestations and attestations, and in the Fulu checks for blocks and data column sidecars. Clients do not follow this text literally, since Fulu blocks propagated, but the next fork will copy it, and test generators that run these functions across a fork will reject valid messages.
en.impact: Minimal preset, fork at epoch 2: the proposer signature of a valid initial Gloas block is invalid when checked with the head state, as the text says, and valid when checked with the state of the block.
en.correction: Compute the domain from the fork version of the epoch of the message, as was done for proposer preferences, in each of the listed checks.

findings.location: Gloas honest builder guide (onboarding note) against the Electra and Gloas beacon chain

en.title: Gloas: the builder onboarding note describes a deposit window that is empty unless the deposit queue has a backlog
en.summary: The honest builder guide says a builder can be onboarded at the fork with a deposit made late enough to be still pending at the fork, but early enough that its slot is finalized, so that the builder is active. Without a backlog in the pending deposit queue no slot meets both conditions: Fulu applies every pending deposit up to the finalized slot, and a builder is active only if its deposit epoch is before the finalized epoch. A deposit that is early enough is applied by Fulu as a validator with a 0xB0 credential, which is not an execution withdrawal credential, so the validator never gets withdrawals. A deposit that is late enough becomes a builder that is not active at the fork. The activation note of the same guide is correct as a condition.
en.impact: Minimal preset, fork at epoch 6, finalized epoch 4 at the upgrade: a deposit in slot 31 becomes validator 64 with a 0xB0 credential and a balance of 32 ETH, and no builder; a deposit in slot 33 becomes builder 0, which is not active at the fork.
en.correction: Tell builders to deposit in the last epoch before the fork, so that the deposit is still pending at the fork and the builder becomes active about two epochs later, and warn that a deposit applied before the fork creates a validator that cannot withdraw. Making builders active from the fork slot would need a change of the rule, which is a design choice.

quotes.text: Builders may be onboarded at the fork by submitting a deposit to the validator deposit contract with a `BUILDER_WITHDRAWAL_PREFIX` withdrawal credential. This must be done late enough that the deposit is still pending at the fork, but early enough that the slot in which the deposit is added to the pending deposit queue is finalized so that the builder is considered active.

findings.location: Gloas and Fulu networking: data column request and response

en.title: Gloas networking: the data column request protocols are not updated for the new data column sidecar
en.summary: Gloas removes the signed block header, the KZG commitments and the inclusion proof from DataColumnSidecar and adds the slot and the beacon block root. The Gloas request and response section updates the block request protocols with a Gloas row, but says nothing about DataColumnSidecarsByRange and DataColumnSidecarsByRoot, which stay as defined in Fulu. Their context epoch is read from the signed block header, their type table maps every epoch from the Fulu fork on to the Fulu sidecar, and the reader is told to check the inclusion proof, which a Gloas sidecar does not have.
en.impact: For a response that carries a Gloas sidecar the text gives no context epoch, no type and no applicable check, so each client has to choose them on its own.
en.correction: Add Gloas sections for both protocols: the context epoch from the slot of the sidecar, a type table with a Gloas row, and checks that take the KZG commitments from the bid of the block named by the beacon block root, with no inclusion proof.

findings.location: EIP-7732, Fork transition, against Gloas fork logic

en.title: EIP-7732: the fork onboarding text still excludes keys of existing validators
en.summary: EIP-7732 says that at the fork, pending deposits with the builder withdrawal prefix are converted to builders only if their public key does not belong to an existing or pending validator. Pull request 5736 in the consensus specifications, merged on 26 October 2026, changed the onboarding function on purpose: a valid builder deposit registers or tops up a builder even if a validator uses the same key, and a builder deposit for an existing builder tops it up regardless of signature. For a key that already belongs to a validator, the EIP now says the opposite of the specification.
en.impact: A pending deposit with the builder prefix and a valid signature, for the key of an existing validator: by the EIP it is not converted; by the specification it registers a builder.
en.correction: Reword the sentence to match the specification: a builder deposit tops up the builder with the same key; otherwise it registers a new builder if its signature is valid, even if a validator uses the same key; other deposits stay in the validator queue.

findings.location: Fetch, determine the same-site mode, steps 2 and 3

en.title: Fetch: the Lax exception for cross-site navigations cannot be reached
en.summary: The check for a cross-site navigation initiator runs before the check for a top-level GET document. A cross-site link therefore never reaches the step meant for it, and that step catches same-site navigations instead. By the text, a Lax cookie is not sent on a cross-site link and a Strict cookie is not sent on a same-origin link.
en.impact: A link from site a to site b, GET: by the text the SameSite=Lax cookie is not sent; Chromium 156, Firefox 157 and WebKit 27.2 send it. A same-origin link, GET: by the text the SameSite=Strict cookie is not sent; all three send it.
en.correction: Decide cross-site GET navigations before the general cross-site case, and give other navigations the full mode.

findings.location: Fetch, determine the same-site mode, steps 4 to 6

en.title: Fetch: cross-site subresources and redirected POST requests get the highest same-site mode
en.summary: No step compares a request with its client. The ancestor check looks at parents only, so a first request from a top-level page on a to b reaches the last step. The redirect check skips a hop when the origin of the request is same site with the URL before it, so a form POST from a to a that redirects to b reaches the last step too.
en.impact: An image, frame or credentialed fetch from a top-level page on a to b: by the text SameSite=Strict and SameSite=Lax cookies are sent; Chromium 156 and Firefox 157 do not send them. A top-level form POST from a to a with a 307 to b: by the text they are sent; Chromium 156, Firefox 157 and WebKit 27.2 do not send them. Existing web-platform-tests in cookies/samesite expect the browser result.
en.correction: Compare the request with its client for non-navigation requests, and count every hop of the URL list.

en.title: Fetch: the same-site algorithm states that every request is GET or POST
en.summary: The first step of the algorithm states as an invariant that the method is GET or POST, but the algorithm also runs for every other method. findings.location: Fetch, Set-Cookie processing, with layered-cookies, Requirements Specific to Browser User Agents

en.title: Fetch: nothing removes expired cookies unless a Set-Cookie response is processed
en.summary: layered-cookies leaves the removal of expired cookies in browsers to Fetch and other callers, and its retrieval steps have no expiry condition. Fetch calls the garbage collection steps only while processing Set-Cookie. If no such response is processed after a cookie expires, the steps return that cookie. The Fetch review of the integration already mentioned clearing cookies periodically, but the list of remaining pieces does not.
en.impact: A cookie with Max-Age=2, then a request 4 seconds later with no response in between: by the steps it is returned; Chromium 156, Firefox 157 and WebKit 27.2 do not send it.
en.correction: Add a call to remove expired cookies in Fetch and the other callers.

en.title: layered-cookies: cookies are sorted by the number of path segments, not by path length
en.summary: Retrieve Cookies sorts by the size of the path, which is its number of segments. RFC 6265bis-22 sorts by length. The root path and a one-segment path have the same size, so creation time decides between them. An existing web-platform-test expects the longer path first.
en.impact: a=1; Path=/, then b=2; Path=/foo, request to /foo/bar: by the steps a=1; b=2; Chromium 156, Firefox 157 and WebKit 27.2 send b=2; a=1. Paths /a/ and /a/b: by the steps creation order; all three put /a/b first.
en.correction: Sort by path length, which is the size of the path plus the lengths of its segments.

quotes.source: draft-ietf-httpbis-layered-cookies (httpwg/http-extensions, commit f9f079a)
quotes.text: Cookies whose path's size is greater are listed before cookies whose path's size is smaller.

en.title: EIP-7928: the text does not say that a static-context halt comes before pre-state validation
en.summary: EIP-7928 says that once pre-state validation passes, the target is accessed and included in the block access list. It does not mention a static context. Take a call with value inside a static frame, with enough gas: pre-state validation passes, so by the text the target goes in the list. The execution specification halts such a call before any gas check, and its test requires the target to stay out of the list. The other state-accessing instructions that a static frame does not allow follow the same order.
en.impact: A call with value inside a static frame, with enough gas: by the EIP the target is in the block access list; by the execution specification and its test it is not. Three coding agents wrote the inclusion check from the current text and all three recorded the target. In three runs with an earlier draft of the proposed paragraph, none did.
en.correction: Add a paragraph after the pre-state validation rule: a state-accessing instruction that a static context does not allow halts before pre-state validation, no gas check applies, and the target stays out of the list unless it was accessed for another reason. Proposed in pull request 12611.

en.title: EIP-8038 and EIP-7928: the pre-state gas of contract creation is left open
en.summary: The pre-state validation table of EIP-7928 lists costs in addition to the base cost of the instruction and uses the older gas constant for contract creation. EIP-8038 replaces that constant with an access charge, which is also the base cost, plus a separate state gas charge, and its section on EIP-7928 does not mention the table. Read together, the two leave the pre-state amount open: a reader can add the access charge twice, or can add the state gas charge. The execution specification charges the access charge once, together with memory expansion and the init code cost. In pull request 12418, closed in October 2026, an author of EIP-7928 wrote that it would not depend on EIP-8038, so the mapping belongs in EIP-8038.
en.impact: Contract creation under both EIPs: by one reading the access charge is counted twice, by another the state gas charge is added, while the execution specification counts the access charge once. Coding agents wrote correct code from the current text, and all three runs asked about this table. With an earlier draft of the proposed paragraph, one of three still did.
en.correction: Add a paragraph to the section of EIP-8038 on EIP-7928 that maps the names in the table to the constants of EIP-8038: the access charge is counted once, the extra warm access of the two code-reading instructions is part of pre-state validation, and state gas is not. Proposed in pull request 12612.

en.title: EIP-7708: the transfer log rules do not cover contract-creation transactions and failed frames
en.summary: The list in EIP-7708 covers a value transaction to a different account and the two creation instructions. It does not name a transaction with an empty recipient field, and the execution specification emits the log for it. The Specification section also does not say what happens to the log when a frame fails; only the Test Cases section lists reverts and rolled-back inner calls among the cases with no log. The execution specification drops the log with the failed frame or an enclosing one, and a creation that fails on an address collision emits no log, because the check comes before the transfer.
en.impact: A contract-creation transaction with value: the list does not cover it, while the execution specification and its test emit the log. A call with value that succeeds inside a frame that later reverts: the Specification section is silent, while the execution specification discards the log. Coding agents wrote correct code from the current text, and all three runs raised these cases. With an earlier draft of the proposed text, one of three still did.
en.correction: Add contract-creation transactions to the list, say that a transfer log belongs to the frame in which the transfer executes and is discarded if that frame or an enclosing frame fails, and say that a transaction that fails before its value transfer emits no log. Proposed in pull request 12613, which also asks the authors whether the log of a contract-creation transaction is meant to be free.

en.title: Environmental Protection Agency: 28 references to former U.S. Code sections or former act names (40 CFR, chapter I, parts 2 to 80)
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Environmental Protection Agency in 40 CFR, chapter I, parts 2 to 80, 28 references in 17 sections use a former address or name: 16 cite a section transferred to another section; 8 cite a repealed section; 3 cite a section replaced by a new one when the title was enacted as positive law; 1 cites a section omitted from the Code. Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code, which names where the old number went.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references finds a note that the section moved, or no section, instead of the text. A reference to a moved section may keep its legal effect, but the address no longer leads to the text. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides how to update each reference. Where the U.S. Code names the section the old number moved to, the evidence below gives it.

en.title: Department of the Interior: 94 references to U.S. Code sections repealed, omitted or not in the Code (43 CFR)
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of the Interior in 43 CFR, 94 references in 69 sections cite a U.S. Code section that release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code does not carry in force: 55 cite a repealed section; 22 cite a section omitted from the Code; 17 cite a number the Code does not have. The release names no successor for these sections.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references does not reach the text the rule relies on. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides whether to remove or replace each reference. The U.S. Code names no successor for these sections.

en.title: Department of Transportation: 241 references to former U.S. Code sections or former act names (14 CFR, chapter I, part 29)
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of Transportation in 14 CFR, chapter I, part 29, 241 references in 50 sections use a former address or name: 241 cite a section replaced by a new one when the title was enacted as positive law. Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code, which names where the old number went.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references finds a note that the section moved, or no section, instead of the text. A reference to a moved section may keep its legal effect, but the address no longer leads to the text. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides how to update each reference. Where the U.S. Code names the section the old number moved to, the evidence below gives it.

en.title: Department of Agriculture: 21 references with a wrong U.S. Code section or act name
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of Agriculture, 21 references in 17 sections cite the U.S. Code or an act with an error: 3 name a U.S. Code section that is not part of the act named next to it; 18 name an act differently from the U.S. Code. Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references reaches a different section or looks for an act under a name the U.S. Code does not use. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides how to correct each reference. Where the U.S. Code shows the section or the name intended, the evidence below gives it.

en.title: Department of the Interior: 11 references with a wrong U.S. Code section or act name
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of the Interior, 11 references in 10 sections cite the U.S. Code or an act with an error: 5 name a U.S. Code section that is not part of the act named next to it; 6 name an act differently from the U.S. Code. Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references reaches a different section or looks for an act under a name the U.S. Code does not use. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides how to correct each reference. Where the U.S. Code shows the section or the name intended, the evidence below gives it.

quotes.text: As applicable, amounts received under this chapter shall be audited in compliance with the Single Audit Act of 1984; (7) after reasonable notice to the government, the government will make available to the Secretary and the Comptroller General of the United States, with the right to inspect, records the Secretary reasonably requires to review compliance with this chapter or the Comptroller General of the United States reasonably requires to review compliance and operations under section 6718(b); (8) the government will make reports the Secretary reasonably requires, in addition to the annual reports required under section 6719(b); and (9) the government will spend the funds only for the purposes set forth in section 6701(a)(2). (e) Review by Governors.-A unit of general local government shall give the chief executive officer of the State in which the government is located an opportunity for review and comment before establishing compliance with subsection (d). (f) Sanctions for Noncompliance.-(1) In general.-If the Secretary decides that a unit of general local government has not complied substantially with subsection (d) or regulations prescribed under subsection (d), the Secretary shall notify the government. The notice shall state that if the government does not take corrective action by the 60th day after the date the government receives the notice, the Secretary will withhold additional payments to the government for the current payment period and later payment periods until the Secretary is satisfied that the government-(A) has taken the appropriate corrective action; and (B) will comply with subsection (d) and regulations prescribed under subsection (d). (2) Notice.-Before giving notice under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall give the chief executive officer of the unit of general local government reasonable notice and an opportunity for comment. (3) Payment conditions.-The Secretary may make a payment to a unit of general local government notified under paragraph (1) only if the Secretary is satisfied that the government-(A) has taken the appropriate corrective action; and (B) will comply with subsection (d) and regulations prescribed under subsection (d). en.title: Department of the Treasury: 21 references with a wrong U.S. Code section or act name
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of the Treasury, 21 references in 17 sections cite the U.S. Code or an act with an error: 1 names a U.S. Code section that is not part of the act named next to it; 20 name an act differently from the U.S. Code. Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references reaches a different section or looks for an act under a name the U.S. Code does not use. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides how to correct each reference. Where the U.S. Code shows the section or the name intended, the evidence below gives it.

quotes.text: tion on the grounds that any provision of, or amendment made by, the United States-Canada Free-Trade Agreement Implementation Act of 1988 implementing the binational panel dispute settlement system under chapter 19 of the Agreement, or the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement Implementation Act implementing the binational panel dispute settlement system under chapter 10 of the USMCA, violates the Constitution may be brought only in the United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit, which shall have jurisdiction of such action. (B) Other constitutional reviewReview is available under subsection (a) with respect to a determination solely concerning a constitutional issue (other than an issue to which subparagraph (A) applies) arising under any law of the United States as enacted or applied. An action for review under this subparagraph shall be assigned to a 3-judge panel of the United States Court of International Trade. (C) Commencement of reviewNotwithstanding the time limits in subsection (a), within 30 days after the date of publication in the Federal Register of notice that binational panel review has been completed, an interested party who is a party to the proceeding in connection with which the matter arises may commence an action under subparagraph (A) or (B) by filing an action in accordance with the rules of the court. (D) Transfer of actions to appropriate courtWhenever an action is filed in a court under subparagraph (A) or (B) and that court finds that the action should have been filed in the other court, the court in which the action was filed shall transfer the action to the other court and the action shall proceed as if it had been filed in the court to which it is transferred on the date upon which it was actually filed in the court from which it is transferred. (E) Frivolous claimsFrivolous claims brought under subparagraph (A) or (B) are subject to dismissal and sanctions as provided under section 1927 of title 28 and the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure. (F) Security(i) Subparagraph (A) actionsThe security requirements of rule 65(c) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure apply with respect to actions commenced under subparagraph (A). (ii) Subparagraph (B) actionsNo claim shall be heard, and no temporary restraining order or temporary or permanent injunction shall be issued, under an action commenced under subparagraph (B), unless the party seeking review first files an undertaking with adequate security in an amount to be fixed by the court sufficient to recompense parties affected for any loss, expense, or damage caused by the improvident or erroneous issuance of such order or injunction. If a court upholds the constitutionality of the determination in question in such action, the court shall award to a prevailing party fees and expenses, in addition to any costs incurred by that party, unless the court finds that the position of the other party was substantially justified or that special circumstances make an award unjust. (G) Panel recordThe record of proceedings before the binational panel shall not be considered part of the record for review pursuant to subparagraph (A) or (B). (H) Appeal to Supreme Court of court orders issued in subparagraph (A) actionsNotwithstanding any other provision of law, any final judgment of the United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit which is issued pursuant to an action brought under subparagraph (A) shall be reviewable by appeal directly to the Supreme Court of the United States. Any such appeal shall be taken by a notice of appeal filed within 10 days after such order is entered; and the jurisdictional statement shall be filed within 30 days after such order is entered. No stay of an order issued pursuant to an action brought under subparagraph (A) may be issued by a single Justice of the Supreme Court. (5) Liquidation of entries(A) ApplicationIn the case of a determination for which binational panel review is requested pursuant to article 1904 of the Agreement or article 10.12 of the USMCA, the rules provided in this paragraph shall apply, notwithstanding the provisions of subsection (c). (B) General ruleIn the case of a determination for which binational panel review is requested pursuant to article 1904 of the Agreement or article 10.12 of the USMCA, entries of merchandise covered by such determination shall be liquidated in accordance with the determination of the administering authority or the Commission, if they are entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for consumption on or before the date of publication in the Federal Register by the administering authority of notice of a final decision of a binational panel, or of an extraordinary challenge committee, not in harmony with that determination. Such notice of a decision shall be published within 10 days of the date of the issuance of the panel or committee decision. (C) Suspension of liquidation(i) In generalNotwithstanding the provisions of subparagraph (B), in the case of a determination described in clause (iii) or (vi) of subsection (a)(2)(B) for which binational panel review is requested pursuant to article 1904 of the Agreement or article 10.12 of the USMCA, the administering authority, upon request of an interested party who was a party to the proceeding in connection with which the matter arises and who is a participant in the binational panel review, shall order the continued suspension of liquidation of those entries of merchandise covered by the determination that are involved in the review pending the final disposition of the review. (ii) NoticeAt the same time as the interested party makes its request to the administering authority under clause (i), that party shall serve a copy of its request on the United States Secretary, the relevant FTA Secretary, and all interested parties who were parties to the proceeding in connection with which the matter arises. (iii) Application of suspensionIf the interested party requesting continued suspension of liquidation under clause (i) is a foreign manufacturer, producer, or exporter, or a United States importer, the continued suspension of liquidation shall apply only to entries of merchandise manufactured, produced, exported, or imported by that particular manufacturer, producer, exporter, or importer. If the interested party requesting the continued suspension of liquidation under clause (i) is an interested party described in subparagraph (C), (D), (E), or (F) of section 1677(9) of this title, the continued suspension of liquidation shall apply only to entries which could be affected by a decision of the binational panel convened under chapter 19 of the Agreement or chapter 10 of the USMCA. (iv) Judicial reviewAny action taken by the administering authority or the United States Customs Service under this subparagraph shall not be subject to judicial review, and no court of the United States shall have power or jurisdiction to review such action on any question of law or fact by an action in the nature of mandamus or otherwise. (6) Injunctive reliefExcept for cases under paragraph (4)(B), in the case of a determination for which binational panel review is requested pursuant to article 1904 of the Agreement or article 10.12 of the USMCA, the provisions of subsection (c)(2) shall not apply. (7) Implementation of international obligations under article 1904 of the Agreement or article 10.12 of the USMCA(A) Action upon remandIf a determination is referred to a binational panel or extraordinary challenge committee under article 1904 of the Agreement or article 10.12 of the USMCA and the panel or committee makes a decision remanding the determination to the administering authority or the Commission, the administering authority or the Commission shall, within the period specified by the panel or committee, take action not inconsistent with the decision of the panel or committee. Any action taken by the administering authority or the Commission under this paragraph shall not be subject to judicial review, and no court of the United States shall have power or jurisdiction to review such action on any question of law or fact by an action in the nature of mandamus or otherwise. (B) Application if subparagraph (A) held unconstitutionalIn the event that the provisions of subparagraph (A) are held unconstitutional under the provisions of subparagraphs (A) and (H) of paragraph (4), the provisions of this subparagraph shall take effect. In such event, the President is authorized on behalf of the United States to accept, as a whole, the decision of a binational panel or extraordinary challenge committee remanding the determination to the administering authority or the Commission within the period specified by the panel or committee. Upon acceptance by the President of such a decision, the administering authority or the Commission shall, within the period specified by the panel or committee, take action not inconsistent with such decision. Any action taken by the President, the administering authority, or the Commission under this subparagraph shall not be subject to judicial review, and no court of the United States shall have power or jurisdiction to review such action on any question of law or fact by an action in the nature of mandamus or otherwise. (8) Requests for binational panel review(A) Interested party requests for binational panel review(i) General ruleAn interested party who was a party to the proceeding in which a determination is made may request binational panel review of such determination by filing a request with the United States Secretary by no later than the date that is 30 days after the date described in subparagraph (A), (B), or (E) of subsection (a)(5) that is applicable to such determination. Receipt of such request by the United States Secretary shall be deemed to be a request for binational panel review within the meaning of article 1904(4) of the Agreement or article 10.12 of the USMCA. Such request shall contain such information and be in such form, manner, and style as the administering authority, in consultation with the Commission, shall prescribe by regulations. (ii) Suspension of time to request binational panel review under the USMCANotwithstanding clause (i), the time for requesting binational panel review shall be suspended during the pendency of any stay of binational panel review that is issued pursuant to article 10.13 of the USMCA. (B) Service of request for binational panel review(i) Service by interested partyIf a request for binational panel review of a determination is filed under subparagraph (A), the party making the request shall serve a copy, by mail or personal service, on any other interested party who was a party to the proceeding in connection with which the matter arises, and on the administering authority or the Commission, as appropriate. (ii) Service by United States SecretaryIf an interested party to the proceeding requests binational panel review of a determination by filing a request with the relevant FTA Secretary, the United States Secretary shall serve a copy of the request by mail on any other interested party who was a party to the proceeding in connection with which the matter arises, and on the administering authority or the Commission, as appropriate. (C) Limitation on request for binational panel reviewAbsent a request by an interested party under subparagraph (A), the United States may not request binational panel review of a determination under article 1904 of the Agreement or article 10.12 of the USMCA. (9) Representation in panel proceedingsIn the case of binational panel proceedings convened under chapter 19 of the Agreement or chapter 10 of the USMCA, the administering authority and the Commission shall be represented by attorneys who are employees of the administering authority or the Commission, respectively. Interested parties who were parties to the proceeding in connection with which the matter arises shall have the right to appear and be represented by counsel before the binational panel. (10) Notification of class or kind rulingsIn the case of a determination which is described in paragraph (2)(B)(vi) of subsection (a) and which is subject to the provisions of paragraph (2), the administering authority, upon request, shall inform any interested person of the date on which the Government of the relevant FTA country received notice of the determination under paragraph 4 of article 1904 of the Agreement or under article 10.12 of the USMCA. (11) Suspension and termination of suspension of article 10.12 of the USMCA(A) SuspensionIf a special committee established under article 10.13 of the USMCA issues an affirmative finding, the Trade Representative may, in accordance with article 10.13 of the USMCA, suspend the operation of article 10.12 of the USMCA. (B) Termination of suspensionIf a special committee is reconvened and makes an affirmative determination described in article 10.13 of the USMCA, any suspension of the operation of article 10.12 of the USMCA shall terminate. (12) Judicial review upon termination of binational panel or committee review under the USMCA(A) Notice of suspension or termination of suspension of article 10.12 of the USMCA(i) Notice of suspensionUpon notification by the Trade Representative or the government of a country described in subparagraph (A) or (B) of subsection (f)(9) that the operation of article 10.12 of the USMCA has been suspended in accordance with article 10.13 of the USMCA, the United States Secretary shall publish in the Federal Register a notice of suspension of article 10.12 of the USMCA. (ii) Notice of termination of suspensionUpon notification by the Trade Representative or the government of a country described in subparagraph (A) or (B) of subsection (f)(9) that the suspension of the operation of article 10.12 of the USMCA is terminated in accordance with article 10.13 of the USMCA, the United States Secretary shall publish in the Federal Register a notice of termination of suspension of article 10.12 of the USMCA. (B) Transfer of final determinations for judicial review upon suspension of article 10.12 of the USMCAIf the operation of article 10.12 of the USMCA is suspended in accordance with article 10.13 of the USMCA-(i) upon the request of an authorized person described in subparagraph (C), any final determination that is the subject of a binational panel review or an extraordinary challenge committee review shall be transferred to the United States Court of International Trade (in accordance with rules issued by the Court) for review under subsection (a); or (ii) in a case in which-(I) a binational panel review was completed fewer than 30 days before the suspension, and (II) extraordinary challenge committee review has not been requested, upon the request of an authorized person described in subparagraph (C) which is made within 60 days after the completion of the binational panel review, the final determination that was the subject of the binational panel review shall be transferred to the United States Court of International Trade (in accordance with rules issued by the Court) for review under subsection (a). (C) Persons authorized to request transfer of final determinations for judicial reviewA request that a final determination be transferred to the Court of International Trade under subparagraph (B) may be made by-(i) if the United States made an allegation under article 10.13 of the USMCA and the operation of article 10.12 of the USMCA was suspended pursuant to article 10.13 of the USMCA-(I) the government of the relevant country described in subparagraph (A) or (B) of subsection (f)(9), (II) an interested party that was a party to the panel or committee review, or (III) an interested party that was a party to the proceeding in connection with which panel review was requested, but only if the time period for filing notices of appearance in the panel review has not expired, or (ii) if a country described in subparagraph (A) or (B) of subsection (f)(9) made an allegation under article 10.13 of the USMCA and the operation of article 10.12 of the USMCA was suspended pursuant to article 10.13 of the USMCA-(I) the government of that country, (II) an interested party that is a person of that country and that was a party to the panel or committee review, or (III) an interested party that is a person of that country and that was a party to the proceeding in connection with which panel review was requested, but only if the time period for filing notices of appearance in the panel review has not expired. (D) Transfer for judicial review upon settlement(i) If the Trade Representative achieves a settlement with the government of a country described in subparagraph (A) or (B) of subsection (f)(9) pursuant to article 10.13 of the USMCA, and referral for judicial review is among the terms of such settlement, any final determination that is the subject of a binational panel review or an extraordinary challenge committee review shall, upon a request described in clause (ii), be transferred to the United States Court of International Trade (in accordance with rules issued by the Court) for review under subsection (a). (ii) A request referred to in clause (i) is a request made by-(I) the country referred to in clause (i), (II) an interested party that was a party to the panel or committee review, or (III) an interested party that was a party to the proceeding in connection with which panel review was requested, but only if the time for filing notices of appearance in the panel review has not expired. en.title: Department of Education: 141 references to U.S. Code sections repealed, omitted or not in the Code
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of Education, 141 references in 128 sections cite a U.S. Code section that release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code does not carry in force: 76 cite a number the Code does not have; 34 cite a section omitted from the Code; 31 cite a repealed section. The release names no successor for these sections.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references does not reach the text the rule relies on. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides whether to remove or replace each reference. The U.S. Code names no successor for these sections.

en.title: Department of Housing and Urban Development: 54 references to U.S. Code sections repealed, omitted or not in the Code
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of Housing and Urban Development, 54 references in 52 sections cite a U.S. Code section that release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code does not carry in force: 34 cite a number the Code does not have; 19 cite a repealed section; 1 cites a section omitted from the Code. The release names no successor for these sections.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references does not reach the text the rule relies on. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides whether to remove or replace each reference. The U.S. Code names no successor for these sections.

en.title: Department of Justice: 75 references to U.S. Code sections repealed, omitted or not in the Code
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of Justice, 75 references in 53 sections cite a U.S. Code section that release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code does not carry in force: 48 cite a repealed section; 26 cite a number the Code does not have; 1 cites a section omitted from the Code. The release names no successor for these sections.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references does not reach the text the rule relies on. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides whether to remove or replace each reference. The U.S. Code names no successor for these sections.

en.title: Department of Transportation: 124 references to U.S. Code sections repealed, omitted or not in the Code
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of Transportation, 124 references in 107 sections cite a U.S. Code section that release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code does not carry in force: 79 cite a number the Code does not have; 44 cite a repealed section; 1 cites a section omitted from the Code. The release names no successor for these sections.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references does not reach the text the rule relies on. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides whether to remove or replace each reference. The U.S. Code names no successor for these sections.

en.title: Department of Veterans Affairs: 56 references to U.S. Code sections repealed, omitted or not in the Code
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of Veterans Affairs, 56 references in 52 sections cite a U.S. Code section that release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code does not carry in force: 32 cite a number the Code does not have; 17 cite a repealed section; 4 cite a vacant number; 3 cite a section omitted from the Code. The release names no successor for these sections.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references does not reach the text the rule relies on. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides whether to remove or replace each reference. The U.S. Code names no successor for these sections.

en.title: Department of the Interior: 59 references to U.S. Code sections repealed, omitted or not in the Code (25 CFR)
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of the Interior in 25 CFR, 59 references in 47 sections cite a U.S. Code section that release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code does not carry in force: 29 cite a section omitted from the Code; 17 cite a number the Code does not have; 13 cite a repealed section. The release names no successor for these sections.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references does not reach the text the rule relies on. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides whether to remove or replace each reference. The U.S. Code names no successor for these sections.

en.title: Department of the Interior: 13 references to U.S. Code sections repealed, omitted or not in the Code (30 CFR)
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of the Interior in 30 CFR, 13 references in 11 sections cite a U.S. Code section that release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code does not carry in force: 8 cite a number the Code does not have; 4 cite a repealed section; 1 cites a section omitted from the Code. The release names no successor for these sections.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references does not reach the text the rule relies on. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides whether to remove or replace each reference. The U.S. Code names no successor for these sections.

en.title: Department of the Treasury: 102 references to U.S. Code sections repealed, omitted or not in the Code (26 CFR)
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of the Treasury in 26 CFR, 102 references in 80 sections cite a U.S. Code section that release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code does not carry in force: 74 cite a repealed section; 22 cite a number the Code does not have; 6 cite a section omitted from the Code. The release names no successor for these sections.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references does not reach the text the rule relies on. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides whether to remove or replace each reference. The U.S. Code names no successor for these sections.

en.title: Department of the Treasury: 26 references to U.S. Code sections repealed, omitted or not in the Code (27 CFR)
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of the Treasury in 27 CFR, 26 references in 21 sections cite a U.S. Code section that release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code does not carry in force: 17 cite a repealed section; 9 cite a number the Code does not have. The release names no successor for these sections.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references does not reach the text the rule relies on. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides whether to remove or replace each reference. The U.S. Code names no successor for these sections.

Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code, which names where the old number went.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references finds a note that the section moved, or no section, instead of the text. A reference to a moved section may keep its legal effect, but the address no longer leads to the text. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides how to update each reference. Where the U.S. Code names the section the old number moved to, the evidence below gives it.

en.title: Department of Defense: 57 references to former U.S. Code sections or former act names (32 CFR, chapter V, parts 536 to 635)
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of Defense in 32 CFR, chapter V, parts 536 to 635, 57 references in 28 sections use a former address or name: 35 cite a renumbered section; 9 cite a section replaced by a new one when the title was enacted as positive law; 7 cite a section transferred to another section; 3 cite a renumbered section; 3 cite a repealed section. Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code, which names where the old number went.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references finds a note that the section moved, or no section, instead of the text. A reference to a moved section may keep its legal effect, but the address no longer leads to the text. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides how to update each reference. Where the U.S. Code names the section the old number moved to, the evidence below gives it.

en.title: Department of Defense: 43 references to former U.S. Code sections or former act names (32 CFR, chapter VI, parts 705 to 770)
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of Defense in 32 CFR, chapter VI, parts 705 to 770, 43 references in 27 sections use a former address or name: 23 cite a renumbered section; 17 cite a section replaced by a new one when the title was enacted as positive law; 1 cites a former appendix not carried in the current Code; 1 cites a repealed section; 1 cites a section transferred to another section. Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code, which names where the old number went.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references finds a note that the section moved, or no section, instead of the text. A reference to a moved section may keep its legal effect, but the address no longer leads to the text. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides how to update each reference. Where the U.S. Code names the section the old number moved to, the evidence below gives it.

en.title: Department of Energy: 46 references to former U.S. Code sections or former act names
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of Energy, 46 references in 38 sections use a former address or name: 19 cite a section replaced by a new one when the title was enacted as positive law; 11 cite a repealed section; 9 cite a section transferred to another section; 6 cite a former appendix not carried in the current Code; 1 cites a renumbered section. Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code, which names where the old number went.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references finds a note that the section moved, or no section, instead of the text. A reference to a moved section may keep its legal effect, but the address no longer leads to the text. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides how to update each reference. Where the U.S. Code names the section the old number moved to, the evidence below gives it.

en.title: Department of Health and Human Services: 4 references to former U.S. Code sections or former act names (2 CFR)

en.title: Department of Health and Human Services: 34 references to former U.S. Code sections or former act names (45 CFR)
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of Health and Human Services in 45 CFR, 34 references in 32 sections use a former address or name: 27 cite a section transferred to another section; 5 cite a section replaced by a new one when the title was enacted as positive law; 2 cite a repealed section. Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code, which names where the old number went.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references finds a note that the section moved, or no section, instead of the text. A reference to a moved section may keep its legal effect, but the address no longer leads to the text. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides how to update each reference. Where the U.S. Code names the section the old number moved to, the evidence below gives it.

en.title: Department of Homeland Security: 3 references to former U.S. Code sections or former act names (31 CFR)
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of Homeland Security in 31 CFR, 3 references in 3 sections use a former address or name: 3 cite a section replaced by a new one when the title was enacted as positive law. Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code, which names where the old number went.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references finds a note that the section moved, or no section, instead of the text. A reference to a moved section may keep its legal effect, but the address no longer leads to the text. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.

en.title: Department of Homeland Security: 17 references to former U.S. Code sections or former act names (44 CFR)
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of Homeland Security in 44 CFR, 17 references in 16 sections use a former address or name: 9 cite a section transferred to another section; 4 cite a former appendix not carried in the current Code; 2 cite a section replaced by a new one when the title was enacted as positive law; 2 cite a repealed section. Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code, which names where the old number went.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references finds a note that the section moved, or no section, instead of the text. A reference to a moved section may keep its legal effect, but the address no longer leads to the text. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides how to update each reference. Where the U.S. Code names the section the old number moved to, the evidence below gives it.

en.title: Department of Labor: 103 references to former U.S. Code sections or former act names (29 CFR)
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of Labor in 29 CFR, 103 references in 62 sections use a former address or name: 80 cite a section replaced by a new one when the title was enacted as positive law; 5 cite a section transferred to another section; 4 cite a renumbered section; 3 cite a repealed section; 2 cite a section omitted from the Code; 2 cite a former appendix not carried in the current Code; 7 name an act by a former name. Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code, which names where the old number went.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references finds a note that the section moved, or no section, instead of the text. A reference to a moved section may keep its legal effect, but the address no longer leads to the text. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides how to update each reference. Where the U.S. Code names the section the old number moved to, the evidence below gives it.
