en.title: Department of Labor: 30 references to former U.S. Code sections or former act names (41 CFR)
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of Labor in 41 CFR, 30 references in 20 sections use a former address or name: 30 cite a section replaced by a new one when the title was enacted as positive law. Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code, which names where the old number went.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references finds a note that the section moved, or no section, instead of the text. A reference to a moved section may keep its legal effect, but the address no longer leads to the text. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides how to update each reference. Where the U.S. Code names the section the old number moved to, the evidence below gives it.

en.title: Department of Transportation: 96 references to former U.S. Code sections or former act names (14 CFR, chapter I, parts 33 to 183)
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of Transportation in 14 CFR, chapter I, parts 33 to 183, 96 references in 39 sections use a former address or name: 92 cite a section replaced by a new one when the title was enacted as positive law; 3 cite a former appendix not carried in the current Code; 1 cites a section omitted from the Code. Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code, which names where the old number went.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references finds a note that the section moved, or no section, instead of the text. A reference to a moved section may keep its legal effect, but the address no longer leads to the text. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides how to update each reference. Where the U.S. Code names the section the old number moved to, the evidence below gives it.

en.title: Department of Transportation: 37 references to former U.S. Code sections or former act names (49 CFR, subtitle A, parts 1 to 91)
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of Transportation in 49 CFR, subtitle A, parts 1 to 91, 37 references in 22 sections use a former address or name: 14 cite a section replaced by a new one when the title was enacted as positive law; 9 cite a former appendix not carried in the current Code; 7 cite a section transferred to another section; 5 cite a repealed section; 2 cite a renumbered section. Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code, which names where the old number went.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references finds a note that the section moved, or no section, instead of the text. A reference to a moved section may keep its legal effect, but the address no longer leads to the text. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides how to update each reference. Where the U.S. Code names the section the old number moved to, the evidence below gives it.

en.title: Department of Transportation: 5 references to former U.S. Code sections or former act names (49 CFR, chapter III, parts 392 to 397)
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of Transportation in 49 CFR, chapter III, parts 392 to 397, 5 references in 5 sections use a former address or name: 3 cite a section replaced by a new one when the title was enacted as positive law; 2 cite a section transferred to another section. Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code, which names where the old number went.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references finds a note that the section moved, or no section, instead of the text. A reference to a moved section may keep its legal effect, but the address no longer leads to the text. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides how to update each reference. Where the U.S. Code names the section the old number moved to, the evidence below gives it.

en.title: Department of Transportation: 100 references to former U.S. Code sections or former act names (49 CFR, chapter V, parts 510 to 593)
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of Transportation in 49 CFR, chapter V, parts 510 to 593, 100 references in 50 sections use a former address or name: 94 cite a repealed section; 6 cite a section replaced by a new one when the title was enacted as positive law. Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code, which names where the old number went.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references finds a note that the section moved, or no section, instead of the text. A reference to a moved section may keep its legal effect, but the address no longer leads to the text. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides how to update each reference. Where the U.S. Code names the section the old number moved to, the evidence below gives it.

en.title: Department of Transportation: 5 references to former U.S. Code sections or former act names (49 CFR, chapter VI, parts 613 to 663)
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of Transportation in 49 CFR, chapter VI, parts 613 to 663, 5 references in 5 sections use a former address or name: 2 cite a renumbered section; 2 cite a section replaced by a new one when the title was enacted as positive law; 1 cites a repealed section. Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code, which names where the old number went.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references finds a note that the section moved, or no section, instead of the text. A reference to a moved section may keep its legal effect, but the address no longer leads to the text. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides how to update each reference. Where the U.S. Code names the section the old number moved to, the evidence below gives it.

en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of Veterans Affairs, 58 references in 45 sections use a former address or name: 15 cite a renumbered section; 15 cite a repealed section; 12 cite a section transferred to another section; 8 cite a renumbered section; 6 cite a section replaced by a new one when the title was enacted as positive law; 2 cite a former appendix not carried in the current Code. Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code, which names where the old number went.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references finds a note that the section moved, or no section, instead of the text. A reference to a moved section may keep its legal effect, but the address no longer leads to the text. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides how to update each reference. Where the U.S. Code names the section the old number moved to, the evidence below gives it.

en.title: Department of the Interior: 7 references to former U.S. Code sections or former act names (2 CFR)

Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code, which names where the old number went.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references finds a note that the section moved, or no section, instead of the text. A reference to a moved section may keep its legal effect, but the address no longer leads to the text. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.

en.title: Department of the Interior: 37 references to former U.S. Code sections or former act names (43 CFR, subtitle A, parts 3 to 100)
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of the Interior in 43 CFR, subtitle A, parts 3 to 100, 37 references in 27 sections use a former address or name: 17 cite a section transferred to another section; 17 cite a repealed section; 3 cite a section omitted from the Code. Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code, which names where the old number went.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references finds a note that the section moved, or no section, instead of the text. A reference to a moved section may keep its legal effect, but the address no longer leads to the text. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides how to update each reference. Where the U.S. Code names the section the old number moved to, the evidence below gives it.

en.title: Department of the Interior: 125 references to former U.S. Code sections or former act names (43 CFR, chapter II, parts 1820 to 9269)
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of the Interior in 43 CFR, chapter II, parts 1820 to 9269, 125 references in 96 sections use a former address or name: 90 cite a section transferred to another section; 21 cite a section replaced by a new one when the title was enacted as positive law; 8 cite a former appendix not carried in the current Code; 6 cite a repealed section. Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code, which names where the old number went.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references finds a note that the section moved, or no section, instead of the text. A reference to a moved section may keep its legal effect, but the address no longer leads to the text. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides how to update each reference. Where the U.S. Code names the section the old number moved to, the evidence below gives it.

en.title: Department of the Treasury: 29 references to former U.S. Code sections or former act names (27 CFR)
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of the Treasury in 27 CFR, 29 references in 22 sections use a former address or name: 24 cite a section replaced by a new one when the title was enacted as positive law; 5 cite a renumbered section. Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code, which names where the old number went.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references finds a note that the section moved, or no section, instead of the text. A reference to a moved section may keep its legal effect, but the address no longer leads to the text. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides how to update each reference. Where the U.S. Code names the section the old number moved to, the evidence below gives it.

en.title: Department of the Treasury: 68 references to former U.S. Code sections or former act names (31 CFR)
en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Department of the Treasury in 31 CFR, 68 references in 57 sections use a former address or name: 39 cite a section replaced by a new one when the title was enacted as positive law; 24 cite a former appendix not carried in the current Code; 4 cite a section transferred to another section; 1 cites a renumbered section. Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code, which names where the old number went.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references finds a note that the section moved, or no section, instead of the text. A reference to a moved section may keep its legal effect, but the address no longer leads to the text. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides how to update each reference. Where the U.S. Code names the section the old number moved to, the evidence below gives it.

en.summary: In the CFR chapters assigned to the Environmental Protection Agency in 40 CFR, chapter I, part 81, 239 references in 237 sections use a former address or name: 239 cite a section transferred to another section. Each reference was compared with release point 119-134 of the U.S. Code, which names where the old number went.
en.impact: A reader who follows these references finds a note that the section moved, or no section, instead of the text. A reference to a moved section may keep its legal effect, but the address no longer leads to the text. No effect on a decision or an amount has been established.
en.correction: The agency decides how to update each reference. Where the U.S. Code names the section the old number moved to, the evidence below gives it.
